Sources: this session's findings (about 30 across PRs #425–#445 and trails #194–#199, #232), the Rust and workflow sweeps run 2026-11-06 (read-only agents, top items re-verified by hand), the `wisp-plugins` repo, and the Caliper and monokl analyses. Labels: VERIFIED = reproduced or read in code by me; AGENT = reported by a sweep agent, not yet checked; UNSURE = needs a real run.

## 1. New verified defects from this round

| # | Defect | Status | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | The generated matrix workflow cannot release: `plan`, `execute` and `build-python` need a detached HEAD, but every `actions/checkout` in `matrix_workflow.tmpl` has no `ref:` | VERIFIED | `callisto release plan` from an attached HEAD exits 1 with E170 "requires a detached HEAD" (real binary, repro test). Template lines 36, 188, 222. Our own `callisto-release.yml` checks out `ref: <sha>`, which is why we never saw it. Fixtures all `checkout --detach`. `init/tests.rs` asserts no `github.sha` in generated workflows and pins golden bytes |
| 2 | Attestation checks pin no source ref; `--signer-ref` does not exist in `gh` 2.103.3 (`--source-ref` does) | VERIFIED | `gh attestation verify --help`. Sites: `install-callisto.sh:119`, `callisto-ci.yml:298`, `release_artifacts.rs:228`. Every stub accepts any flag, so tests would stay green on a wrong flag |
| 3 | pypi observation is an unauthenticated `curl`; publish uses `TWINE_*` | VERIFIED (read) | `pypi.rs:196` vs `pypi.rs:10-28`. Same shape as the npm bug. A private index returns 401 and the release can never preflight or confirm. Not run end to end |
| 4 | Generated templates pin older actions than the repo (upload-artifact v7.0.1 vs v7.0.2, download-artifact v8.0.1 vs v8.0.2); `verify-action-pins.sh` scans only `*.yml` so `.tmpl` is never checked | VERIFIED | grep of SHAs |
| 5 | `run_publish_client` drops the classifier outcome (`.map(\|_outcome\| ())`), so a receipt cannot say "adopted" vs "published"; the text summary prints "Released N package(s)" on a rerun that published nothing | VERIFIED (read) | `registry.rs:152-160`, `release.rs:140-146` |
| 6 | The tag probe reports nothing when `ls-remote` fails, and `handle.join().unwrap_or_default()` turns a probe panic into "nothing missing" | VERIFIED (read); the comment says best effort | `local.rs:119-134`, `release.rs:82-88` |
| 7 | Fake `cargo publish` does not require `--registry`, so dropping it from the real argv would pass the e2e suite | AGENT | `release_harness.rs:913-1006` |
| 8 | The fake git needed the full refspec (fixed in #442), and the fake `ls-remote` matches only exact refs where real git does tail matching | VERIFIED for the first, AGENT for the second | #442 finding, `825ef6248` |
| 9 | `install-callisto.sh:137` silently falls back to `cargo install` from crates.io on any download failure, bypassing `verification=require` | AGENT | lines 127-129, 182-187 |
| 10 | Unpinned dev tools gate the release `verify` job (nextest, cargo-deny, llvm-cov, machete, semver-checks, mutants, nightly) | AGENT | `callisto-release.yml:56,70` |
| 11 | `RELEASE_CREDENTIALS` exists in three diverged lists (`runner.rs:52`, `registry.rs:339`, harness `CREDENTIAL_VARS`) | AGENT | `NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG` vs `CALLISTO_PUBLISH_NPM_CONFIG` |
| 12 | `taiki-e/install-action` pinned to a different SHA in `install-workflow-linters` | AGENT, matches our earlier note | `action.yml:7` |
| 13 | `rate`/`auth`/`429`/`401` substring matching in the rate-limit and auth detectors | AGENT | `registry_argv.rs:461-485`; misleading text only |
| 14 | The CI test matrix executes on 2 of 5 targets, and `macos-latest` floats while the release matrix pins `macos-15` | AGENT | `callisto-ci.yml:113` |
| 15 | `just ci` is a strict subset of GitHub CI | VERIFIED | CI also runs machete, features-boundary, check-api, per-crate coverage, `--locked` check, MSRV, artifact preflight and two contract scripts |

Items from the Rust sweep not repeated above are UNSURE or documented-benign: tag-ownership `unwrap_or(true)` (documented), `resolve_commit` collapsing a malformed SHA (unreachable if E265 gates), npm `workspace:` unreadable target dropping an edge, `root.rs` strict vs lossy existence checks, `repository()` returning `None` for every failure, `build-python` JSON without the report envelope.

The sweeps found no `let _ =` or bare `.ok();` that drops a meaningful result, no unbounded retry, and all three publish classifiers check success first. Those patterns are clean after this round's fixes.

## 2. What the findings have in common (families, not instances)

1. Intent lost across a hop: cargo registry `url`, yarn `--registry`, dispatch skipping `verify`, `Released N` summary, receipt outcome.
2. A sibling path that diverged from its twin: npm observe vs publish auth, pypi observe vs publish auth, `add --dry-run`, matrix template vs our own workflow (detach, pins).
3. Copies and pins with no single owner: runner labels, action SHAs, template pins, credential lists, extension lists (monokl), schema versions (Caliper).
4. Test doubles that encode the old contract: fake git refspec, fake cargo `--registry`, stubs that accept any `gh` flag.
5. Success decided after text, or a claim made before proof: publish classifiers, "fixed" before CI, "done" after lib tests.
6. External state that expires silently: `macos-14`, floating tool versions, `releases/latest`.
7. Generated output not tested as the downstream consumer sees it: the matrix template (E170), template pins, attestation flags.
8. Slop: comments, dead code, hardcoded values.

## 3. Why we make these mistakes

1. We fix the instance. Nothing requires sweeping siblings, doubles, scripts and CI definitions.
2. Fakes are checked against the code, never against the real tool.
3. Verification is narrower than CI (`just ci` is a subset; I ran lib tests on #442 and the e2e suite found the harness bug).
4. Our own repo is the only consumer we test. Fixtures detach, our workflow detaches, so the generated template was never exercised.
5. Pins and lists have no owner or expiry.
6. Reviews see diffs; old code is reviewed only by sweeps.
7. Process lives in memory, not in the repo: this repo's `CLAUDE.md` says nothing about verification parity, sibling sweeps or the plugins. The plugin use is a personal memory rule.
8. Speed and relay: agent summaries were relayed as fact, and I declared fixes before CI had run (recorded twice in the incident memory).

## 4. Are we confident there are no more? No.

Evidence against confidence: each fix this session produced or missed a sibling (#425's own recursion, #442's harness, the BOM note from August still open in November). The sweeps above found new instances in every family within minutes. 137 sweep findings in monokl and many here were dismissed by triage rather than reproduction.

What is not covered yet: the Rust sweep examined about 60 of about 470 silent-fallback hits in depth; `unwrap_or(` was triaged by shape only. The shell sweep did not run `shellcheck` or `actionlint` with every rule. Nothing has exercised the generated simple template end to end. The oracle-style "does it work for a downstream repo" check does not exist.

## 5. Guards, in order of payoff

1. A downstream-consumer test: generate the workflow for a scratch repo, check it out the way `actions/checkout` does (attached HEAD on a branch) and run the plan and execute commands against it. Would have caught E170.
2. Release rehearsal in CI for PRs touching the release workflow, templates or action, with a real build.
3. One `verify` command equal to CI, run clean, and a worker report listing the proving command per claim and the sites searched.
4. Contract tests that run the fakes' argument grammar against the real tool (`gh`, `git`, `cargo`, `npm`): extend `ToolShape` to require flags the product must send (`--registry`, full refspec) and to reject flags the real tool lacks (`--signer-ref`).
5. Single-source checks: runner labels, action SHAs (including `.tmpl`), credential lists, extension-like lists.
6. A scheduled job that checks every runner label and pinned tool version still resolves.
7. A ratchet on `unwrap_or*`, `let _ =`, `|| true`, `.ok()?` that can only go down.
8. Tests must fail on the pre-fix source (do it by hand for each fix until it is a rule).
9. Pin the dev tools the release `verify` job installs.

## 6. The plugins

Read in full this round: Smith skill, Ranger audit skill, Rust hazard and boundary packs, verification evidence and implementation-review references, changeset reference, constitution excerpt, AGENTS.md.

What is already there and sound: defect-family sibling search (syntactic and semantic), mutation gate, boundary testing that names the mocked segment, environment testing including CI configuration, external-state freshness, refutation per hazard, T1/T2/T4/T7/T8/T10 matching our top patterns.

Gaps that explain misses:
- Language coverage is Rust, TypeScript, JavaScript, Python and Go. Smith's review treats any other language as "record a coverage gap", so shell, workflow YAML, templates and `jq` (a large share of our findings) are tolerated gaps by design.
- Fakes: the plugins ask to name the mocked segment but not to validate the fake against the real tool.
- Verification parity with CI is "when relevant", not required.
- Duplicated sources of truth, expiring pins and generated-output-as-consumer are not hazard types.
- Ranger's adversary downgrades external uncertainty to `plausible`, which never blocks. That fits a genuine unknown but would also soften "runner label retired".
- Slop, dead code and hardcoded values are outside Ranger; they came from Entire's reviewer and my agents.
- Courier's `changeset@2` is structured JSON with grouped release notes. Callisto changesets are flat markdown. A mapping step is required before `courier:changeset` output goes into `.changeset/`. Not tried.

Process, not structure: this session mostly used general agents with hand-written briefs, so Smith's reviewer, mutator and exit gate never ran. Your memory rule says to use the plugins; the repo itself does not.

## 7. What belongs in the plugins vs this repo

Generic (plugins): hazard families with signal, confirm and refute; sibling sweep that includes test doubles, scripts and CI definitions; fake-vs-real validation as evidence; verification parity with CI; consumer-view testing of generated output; expiring pins; a shell, workflow and template pack; a worker report that names the proving command per claim.

Callisto-specific (repo data): E-code registry and generated `docs/errors.md`; spec criterion IDs; release flow invariants (draft hold, decision, receipt, detached-HEAD requirement for CI routes); where the fakes live (`release_harness.rs`, `RIG_GIT_TAIL`, `ToolShape`); the `gh` bot-token wrapper and worktree guard quirks; Entire trails; runner labels.

How to stay generic: the plugin states the failure class and the evidence needed; the repo supplies a short hazards and contracts file that recon loads through `<load_first>`. Tests for a new line: would it hold for a Go CLI; does it order steps where order does not matter; does it fix a measured miss (use real misses as `mason:evaluate` fixtures).

## 8. Next, in order

1. Fix E170 in the matrix template (and the action if it should accept attached HEAD): `ref: ${{ github.sha }}` on the plan, build-python and execute checkouts, update `init/tests.rs` and the golden snapshot, add the attached-HEAD regression test, add a downstream-consumer test. Tell monokl.
2. Attestation: replace the planned `--signer-ref` with `--source-ref refs/heads/main` plus `--cert-identity`, run it against the real `gh` once, and make the stub reject unknown flags.
3. `verify` command equal to CI, worker report template.
4. pypi observation auth, receipt outcome (adopted vs published), `Released N` summary.
5. Template pin drift plus extend `verify-action-pins.sh` to `.tmpl`; unify credential lists; pin the release `verify` tools.
6. Pattern sweeps continued with separate verifiers; confirmed backlog (cargo `url`, yarn `--registry`, BOM/CRLF, dispatch `verify`, late npm window, pre-mode, E320, changelog already-written, `overrides`, E167, release-commit path check); cleanup trails #194–#199.
7. `wisp-plugins` PR: shell/CI/template pack, fake-vs-real rule, CI parity, consumer-view check, each backed by a real miss as a fixture.

Yours: Entire gates, resolving findings, merging #445 and updating the open PRs, trail #179 decisions.

The full analysis is saved at `.claude/plans/ANALYSIS-2026-11-review-and-slop-patterns.md` (git-excluded). This round found one blocker for downstream repos, and the answer to "do more issues exist?" is yes. I reproduced it and the other verified items below myself, and I haven't fixed any of them yet.

## New findings (checked by me, not just agents)
1. **The generated matrix workflow cannot release.** `release plan` from an attached HEAD fails on the real binary with E170 "requires a detached HEAD". Every `actions/checkout` in `matrix_workflow.tmpl` has no `ref:`, so `plan`, `execute` and `build-python` all fail in downstream repos. Our own release workflow checks out `ref: <sha>`, which is why we never saw it. This is monokl's 0.3.0 failure, but they hit it on the simple template, which uses `AnyHead` and shouldn't raise E170. It's possible they ran an older Callisto or hit a different E170 precondition; I haven't confirmed which.
2. **The attestation fix I'd planned would have broken.** `gh` 2.103.3 has `--source-ref` but no `--signer-ref`, and every stub accepts any flag, so tests would have stayed green on a wrong flag.
3. **pypi observation is an unauthenticated `curl`** while publish uses `TWINE_*`. A private index would return 401 and the release could never preflight or confirm. This is the same shape as the npm bug. I confirmed it by reading the code, not by running it.
4. **Template pins have drifted** (upload-artifact v7.0.1 vs v7.0.2, download-artifact v8.0.1 vs v8.0.2), and `verify-action-pins.sh` never scans `.tmpl` files.
5. **The publish classifier's `AlreadyPublished` result is thrown away**, and a rerun that published nothing still prints "Released N package(s)".
6. **`just ci` is a strict subset of GitHub CI**, which explains "green locally, red in CI".

Agent-reported but not yet verified: the fake `cargo publish` ignores `--registry`, and `install-callisto.sh` silently falls back to `cargo install`. The release `verify` job also runs unpinned tools, and three diverged `RELEASE_CREDENTIALS` lists exist. These are in the file with their status.

## What the findings share
- **The recurring failures:** intent lost across a hop, sibling paths that diverge, copies and pins with no owner, fakes that encode the old contract, success judged after text, and external state that expires. The new one is generated output never tested as a downstream consumer sees it.
- **Why they keep happening:** we fix the instance and not the family. Fakes are never checked against the real tool, and verification is narrower than CI. Process lives in my memory notes, not in this repo's `CLAUDE.md`.

## Are we confident there are no more? No.
- Each fix this session produced or missed a sibling.
- Both sweeps found new instances in minutes.
- The Rust sweep read about 60 of roughly 470 silent-fallback hits in depth.
- Nothing yet runs the generated workflow the way a downstream repo does.

## Plugins
- **What's sound:** sibling search, a mutation gate, boundary testing, and hazards with refutation (T1, T2, T4, T7, T8, T10) that match our top patterns.
- **Gaps:**
  - Shell, workflow YAML and templates are an accepted "coverage gap" by design.
  - Fakes aren't validated against the real tool.
  - CI parity is optional.
  - Consumer-view testing is missing.
  - Ranger can't see the slop patterns.
- **Process miss:** I mostly bypassed Smith's reviewer, mutator and exit gate this session.
- **Not yet checked:** courier's changeset format doesn't match Callisto's flat bullets. I read the reference file but haven't tried a mapping.

## What goes where
- **Plugins:** hazard families, the sibling sweep including fakes and CI, fake-vs-real validation, CI parity, consumer-view testing, and a shell/workflow/template pack.
- **This repo, as data:** the E-codes, spec IDs, release invariants, where the fakes live and runner labels.
- **Staying generic:** the plugin states the failure class and the evidence needed, and the repo supplies a short hazards file that recon loads. The test for any new line is whether it would hold for a Go CLI and fix a measured miss.

## Next
1. Fix E170 in the matrix template: add `ref: ${{ github.sha }}`, update the golden snapshot, add the attached-HEAD regression test, and tell monokl.
2. Fix attestation with `--source-ref` plus `--cert-identity`, run it once against the real `gh`, and make the stub reject unknown flags.
3. Write the CI-equal `verify` command and the worker report template.
4. Fix pypi observation auth and the receipt outcome.
5. Pin the template and `verify` tools, and unify the credential lists.
6. Continue the confirmed backlog and the `wisp-plugins` PR.

Shall I start with E170? I can publish this as a shareable page if you want it to travel with the other analyses.

build-python:
    needs: plan
    if: needs.plan.outputs.release == 'true' && needs.plan.outputs.has_python == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions: {contents: read}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with: {fetch-depth: 0, persist-credentials: false}
      - uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/setup-callisto@__COMMIT__ # callisto@__VERSION__
        with: {version: callisto@__VERSION__}
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
      - name: Build the Python distributions
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          python3 -m venv "$RUNNER_TEMP/build-venv"
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/build-venv/bin/python" -m pip install --quiet __BUILD__
          export PATH="$RUNNER_TEMP/build-venv/bin:$PATH"
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/python-dist"
          callisto release build-python --intent "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json" \
            --artifact-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/python-dist"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: python-dist
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/python-dist/*
          if-no-files-found: error

  execute:
    needs: [plan, build, build-python]
    # A skipped build blocks only when it had nothing to build.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.plan.outputs.release == 'true' &&
      (needs.build.result == 'success' || (needs.build.result == 'skipped' && needs.plan.outputs.matrix == '[]')) &&
      (needs.build-python.result == 'success' || (needs.build-python.result == 'skipped' && needs.plan.outputs.has_python != 'true'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    concurrency: {group: callisto-release-execute, cancel-in-progress: false}
    permissions: {contents: write, id-token: write, attestations: read}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with: {fetch-depth: 0} # zizmor: ignore[artipacked] tag push needs persisted credentials
      - uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/setup-callisto@__COMMIT__ # callisto@__VERSION__
        with: {version: callisto@__VERSION__}
      - name: Install twine
        if: needs.plan.outputs.has_python == 'true'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Installs or builds the Callisto binary. Factored out of action.yml so
# callisto-action's own environment setup can call it directly by path
# (github.action_path has no ref-ambiguous `uses:` to resolve), instead of
# duplicating this logic.
set -euo pipefail

# Install into $RUNNER_TEMP so the binary never lands inside the workspace
# tree (preventing accidental git-staging by downstream steps that run
# "git add -A").
CALLISTO_BIN_DIR="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-bin"
mkdir -p "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR"
TAG_NAME="$INPUT_CALLISTO_VERSION"
SOURCE="$INPUT_CALLISTO_SOURCE"

if [[ "$SOURCE" != "auto" && "$SOURCE" != "local" ]]; then
  echo "::error::unsupported setup-callisto source '$SOURCE' (expected auto or local)"
  exit 1
fi

# With no explicit version override, install the release this action's own
# invocation is pinned to (GITHUB_ACTION_REF, github.action_ref) rather than
# whatever is newest, so `callisto-action@<sha> # callisto@X.Y.Z` always
# installs X.Y.Z. Falls back to true "latest" when the ref is unset (local or
# unpinned invocation) or matches no published callisto@ tag; a failed tag
# lookup fails the step. A named ref such as the floating `v1` tag stands for
# the commit it points at.
if [[ "$SOURCE" == "auto" && "$TAG_NAME" == "latest" && -n "${GITHUB_ACTION_REF:-}" ]]; then
  if ! remote_tags=$(git ls-remote --tags https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto.git 'callisto@*' "$GITHUB_ACTION_REF"); then
    echo "::error::could not list callisto release tags to resolve action ref $GITHUB_ACTION_REF; set the version input to install a specific release"
    exit 1
  fi
  ref_commit=$(printf '%s\n' "$remote_tags" \
    | awk -v ref="refs/tags/$GITHUB_ACTION_REF" '$2 == ref || $2 == ref "^{}" { sha = $1 } END { print sha }')
  resolved_tag=$(printf '%s\n' "$remote_tags" \
    | awk -v ref="${ref_commit:-$GITHUB_ACTION_REF}" '$1 == ref && $2 ~ /^refs\/tags\/callisto@/ { print $2 }' \
    | sed -e 's#^refs/tags/##' -e 's/\^{}$//' \
    | sort -V | tail -n1) || true
  if [[ -n "$resolved_tag" ]]; then
    echo "Resolved action ref $GITHUB_ACTION_REF to $resolved_tag"
    TAG_NAME="$resolved_tag"
  fi
fi

# Validate verification mode
VERIFICATION="${INPUT_CALLISTO_VERIFICATION:-fallback}"
case "$VERIFICATION" in
  require|fallback|skip) ;;
  *)
    echo "::error::unsupported setup-callisto verification '$VERIFICATION' (valid values: require, fallback, skip)"
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

# Detect OS platform architecture for pre-built binaries
OS_NAME=$(uname -s | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
ARCH_NAME=$(uname -m)

if [[ "$OS_NAME" == "darwin" ]]; then
  case "$ARCH_NAME" in
    arm64) ASSET_NAME="callisto-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz" ;;
    x86_64) ASSET_NAME="callisto-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.gz" ;;
    *) ASSET_NAME="" ;;
  esac
elif [[ "$OS_NAME" == "linux" ]]; then
  case "$ARCH_NAME" in
    x86_64) ASSET_NAME="callisto-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz" ;;
    aarch64 | arm64) ASSET_NAME="callisto-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz" ;;
    *) ASSET_NAME="" ;;
  esac
elif [[ "$OS_NAME" == *"mingw"* || "$OS_NAME" == *"msys"* || "$OS_NAME" == *"windows"* ]]; then
  ASSET_NAME=""
else
  ASSET_NAME=""
fi

if [[ -n "$ASSET_NAME" && "$TAG_NAME" == "latest" ]]; then
  DOWNLOAD_URL="https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/releases/latest/download/$ASSET_NAME"
elif [[ -n "$ASSET_NAME" ]]; then
  DOWNLOAD_URL="https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/releases/download/$TAG_NAME/$ASSET_NAME"
fi

# Derive a crates.io version spec from TAG_NAME: "latest" installs
# whatever crates.io resolves as latest (no --version flag); an
# explicit tag ("callisto@0.5.0" or legacy "callisto-cli@0.5.0")
# strips either prefix down to the bare semver cargo install expects.
CRATE_VERSION="${TAG_NAME#callisto@}"; CRATE_VERSION="${CRATE_VERSION#callisto-cli@}"

# Pick a download destination whose extension matches ASSET_NAME
# (under $RUNNER_TEMP, never the workspace) so the extraction step
# below always has an archive it can actually open -- a hardcoded
# ".tar.gz" path here previously masked the fact that Windows assets
# are zip files, since tar -xzf can't read a zip regardless of what
# the file on disk is really named.
case "$ASSET_NAME" in
  *.zip)
    DOWNLOAD_DEST="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto.zip"
    ;;
  *.tar.gz)
    DOWNLOAD_DEST="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto.tar.gz"
    ;;
  *)
    DOWNLOAD_DEST="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto.tar.gz"
    ;;
esac

# A prebuilt asset runs with the job's privileges, so it must carry a
# GitHub attestation from the Callisto release workflow before it is
# extracted. require aborts on failure; fallback discards the asset and
# returns 1 so the crates.io path runs; skip trusts the asset.
verify_asset() {
  local reason=""
  if [[ "$VERIFICATION" == "skip" ]]; then
    echo "::warning::verification=skip: $ASSET_NAME was not verified"
    return 0
  fi
  if ! command -v gh >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    reason="gh is not installed"
  elif ! gh attestation verify "$DOWNLOAD_DEST" \
      --repo orin-dx/callisto \
      --signer-workflow orin-dx/callisto/.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml \
      --deny-self-hosted-runners; then
    reason="attestation verification failed"
  fi
  [[ -z "$reason" ]] && return 0
  rm -f "$DOWNLOAD_DEST"
  if [[ "$VERIFICATION" == "require" ]]; then
    echo "::error::cannot verify $ASSET_NAME: $reason (verification=require)"
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "::warning::cannot verify $ASSET_NAME: $reason; discarding it and installing from crates.io (verification=fallback)"
  return 1
}

# Download, verify and extract the prebuilt asset; nonzero means use the fallback chain.
fetch_prebuilt() {
  curl -sL -f "$DOWNLOAD_URL" -o "$DOWNLOAD_DEST" 2>/dev/null || return 1
  verify_asset || return 1
  # Extract only the expected binary, never the whole archive.
  case "$ASSET_NAME" in
    *.zip)
      unzip -q "$DOWNLOAD_DEST" callisto.exe -d "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR"
      ;;
    *)
      tar -xzf "$DOWNLOAD_DEST" -C "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR" callisto
      ;;
  esac
}

# Dependencies named callisto-cli do not establish checkout source ownership.
owns_local_source() {
  local workspace git_root metadata
  workspace=$(cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" && pwd -P) || return 1
  git_root=$(git -C "$workspace" rev-parse --show-toplevel) || return 1
  [[ "$git_root" == "$workspace" ]] || return 1
  git -C "$workspace" ls-files --error-unmatch -- \
    Cargo.toml crates/callisto-cli/Cargo.toml crates/callisto-cli/src/main.rs >/dev/null || return 1
  metadata=$(cargo metadata --locked --offline --no-deps --format-version 1 \
    --manifest-path "$workspace/Cargo.toml") || return 1
  jq -e --arg workspace "$workspace" '
    .workspace_root == $workspace and
    (.workspace_members as $members | [.packages[] |
      select(.name == "callisto-cli" and .source == null and
        .manifest_path == ($workspace + "/crates/callisto-cli/Cargo.toml") and
        (.id as $id | $members | index($id) != null) and
        any(.targets[]; .name == "callisto" and (.kind | index("bin") != null) and
          .src_path == ($workspace + "/crates/callisto-cli/src/main.rs")))] | length == 1)
  ' <<< "$metadata" >/dev/null
}

if [[ "$SOURCE" == "local" ]]; then
  if ! owns_local_source; then
    echo "::error::setup-callisto source=local requires a Callisto workspace checkout; check out Callisto source or use source=auto"
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "Building local callisto binary from current repository commit..."
  cargo build --locked --manifest-path "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/Cargo.toml" -p callisto-cli \
    --bin callisto --target-dir "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/target"
  cp "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/target/debug/callisto" "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR/callisto"
elif [[ -n "$ASSET_NAME" ]] && fetch_prebuilt; then
  echo "Callisto downloaded from GitHub Releases ($DOWNLOAD_URL)"
elif [[ "$TAG_NAME" == "latest" ]] && cargo install callisto-cli --locked --root "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install" --quiet; then
  echo "Callisto installed from crates.io (latest)"
  cp "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install/bin/callisto" "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR/callisto"
elif [[ "$TAG_NAME" != "latest" ]] && cargo install callisto-cli --version "$CRATE_VERSION" --locked --root "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install" --quiet; then
  echo "Callisto installed from crates.io ($CRATE_VERSION)"
  cp "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install/bin/callisto" "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR/callisto"
else
  echo "::error::callisto $TAG_NAME is available neither as a prebuilt asset nor on crates.io"
  exit 1
fi

echo "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR" >> $GITHUB_PATH
if [[ -f "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.github/callisto-problem-matcher.json" ]]; then
  echo "::add-matcher::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.github/callisto-problem-matcher.json"
fi

# GITHUB_WORKSPACE points at an empty temp dir (no Cargo.toml present, so the
# local-monorepo-build branch is always skipped here) and RUNNER_TEMP /
# CALLISTO_BIN_DIR / GITHUB_PATH point at temp paths.
run_case() {
  local uname_s="$1"
  local uname_m="$2"
  local curl_exit="$3"
  local gh_mode="${4:-ok}"
  local mode="${5-}"
  local tag="${6:-latest}"
  local calls_file workspace runner_temp bin_dir github_path tmp_script
  calls_file="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/callisto.XXXXXX")"
  workspace="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/callisto.XXXXXX")"
  runner_temp="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/callisto.XXXXXX")"
  bin_dir="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/callisto.XXXXXX")"
  github_path="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/callisto.XXXXXX")"
  tmp_script="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/callisto.XXXXXX")"
  local isolated_path
  isolated_path="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/callisto.XXXXXX")"
  for d in "$workspace" "$runner_temp" "$bin_dir" "$isolated_path"; do
    [[ -n "$d" && -d "$d" ]] || { echo "mktemp -d failed" >&2; exit 1; }
  done
  for t in tr grep rm; do ln -s "$(command -v "$t")" "$isolated_path/$t"; done
  {
    printf 'uname() {\n'
    printf '  case "$1" in\n'
    printf '    -s) echo %q ;;\n' "$uname_s"
    printf '    -m) echo %q ;;\n' "$uname_m"
    printf '    *) return 99 ;;\n'
    printf '  esac\n'
    printf '}\n'
    printf 'curl() { echo "curl $*" >> %q; [[ %q -eq 0 ]] && : > "${@: -1}"; return %q; }\n' "$calls_file" "$curl_exit" "$curl_exit"
    printf 'tar() { echo "tar $*" >> %q; return 0; }\n' "$calls_file"
    printf 'unzip() { echo "unzip $*" >> %q; return 0; }\n' "$calls_file"
    printf 'cargo() { echo "cargo $*" >> %q; return 0; }\n' "$calls_file"
    printf 'cp() { echo "cp $*" >> %q; return 0; }\n' "$calls_file"
    printf 'git() { echo "unexpected git $*" >> %q; return 99; }\n' "$calls_file"
    case "$gh_mode" in
      ok) printf 'gh() { echo "gh $*" >> %q; return 0; }\n' "$calls_file" ;;
      fail) printf 'gh() { echo "gh $*" >> %q; return 1; }\n' "$calls_file" ;;
      missing) printf 'PATH=%q\n' "$isolated_path" ;;
    esac
    [[ -n "$mode" ]] && printf 'INPUT_CALLISTO_VERIFICATION=%q\n' "$mode"
    printf 'GITHUB_WORKSPACE=%q\n' "$workspace"
    printf 'RUNNER_TEMP=%q\n' "$runner_temp"
    printf 'CALLISTO_BIN_DIR=%q\n' "$bin_dir"
    printf 'GITHUB_PATH=%q\n' "$github_path"
    printf 'TAG_NAME=%q\n' "$tag"

The installer and the CI attestation job verified Callisto's release assets against the repository and the release workflow, but not against a ref, so an asset attested from another branch or a manual dispatch would pass. Both now add `--source-ref refs/heads/main`. The product's own artifact check already pins the signer digest and source digest and is unchanged.

Checked against the real `gh` 2.103.3 and real assets: the flag verifies the 12 most recent releases (0.10.0 to 0.17.0), a wrong ref fails with `expected SourceRepositoryRef to be refs/heads/nope, got refs/heads/main`, and `--signer-ref`, which an earlier plan used, does not exist and is rejected. The installer test's `gh` stub now rejects any flag the real command lacks (swapping in `--signer-ref` fails 10 of its cases), and the CI job gains a wrong-ref negative control. actionlint shows only the known `$/` self-reference diagnostic, and zizmor and the workflow policy check pass.

Not checked: a run of the CI job itself, which needs this change on `main`.

17:- **Scoped npm packages** publish with `--access public` by default. A private scoped package sets `publishConfig.access` to `"restricted"` in its `package.json`, which Callisto passes through.
38:A registry with no `url` in `callisto.toml` publishes wherever the checkout's own configuration says: `.npmrc` for npm and `.cargo/config.toml` for Cargo. Callisto honors that on purpose, so a private registry set there keeps working, and it means those files decide where the registry token is sent. Review changes to them like code. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# Local actions are commit-bound by the checkout. Every external GitHub action
# must use its full immutable commit hash; Docker actions must use an immutable
# content digest. The generated-workflow templates are checked too, and one
# action resolves to one commit across the repository and its templates.
set -euo pipefail

status=0
declare -A pinned
while IFS= read -r line; do
  reference=${line#*uses: }
  reference=${reference%% #*}
  reference=${reference//[[:space:]]/}
  # Workspace-relative and GitHub's self-repository references are bound to
  # local repository content; only external actions need an explicit pin.
  [[ "$reference" == ./* || "$reference" == '$/'* ]] && continue
  # A template placeholder is replaced with a commit when the workflow is rendered.
  [[ "$reference" =~ @__[A-Z_]+__$ ]] && continue
  if [[ "$reference" == docker://* ]]; then
    valid='^docker://[^@[:space:]]+@sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$'
  else
    valid='^[^@[:space:]]+@[0-9a-f]{40}$'
  fi
  if [[ ! "$reference" =~ $valid ]]; then
    printf 'mutable or malformed external action reference: %s\n' "$line" >&2
    status=1
    continue
  fi
  name=${reference%@*}
  commit=${reference##*@}
  if [[ -n "${pinned[$name]:-}" && "${pinned[$name]}" != "$commit" ]]; then
    printf '%s is pinned to two commits: %s and %s\n' "$name" "${pinned[$name]}" "$commit" >&2
    status=1
  fi
  pinned[$name]=$commit
done < <(rg --no-heading --no-filename --glob '*.yml' --glob '*.yaml' --glob '*.tmpl' '^\s*(- )?uses:\s*' .github crates/callisto-graph/src/templates)
codeowners=.github/CODEOWNERS
if [[ ! -f "$codeowners" ]] \
  || ! rg -q '^/\.github/workflows/\s+@[^[:space:]]+$' "$codeowners" \
  || ! rg -q '^/\.github/actions/\s+@[^[:space:]]+$' "$codeowners"; then
  printf 'CODEOWNERS must cover .github/workflows/ and .github/actions/ with a real owner\n' >&2
  status=1
fi
exit "$status"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Local actions are commit-bound by the checkout. Every external GitHub action
3	# must use its full immutable commit hash; Docker actions must use an immutable
4	# content digest.
5	set -euo pipefail
6	
7	status=0
8	while IFS= read -r line; do
9	  reference=${line#*uses: }
10	  reference=${reference%% #*}
11	  reference=${reference//[[:space:]]/}
12	  # Workspace-relative and GitHub's self-repository references are bound to
13	  # local repository content; only external actions need an explicit pin.
14	  [[ "$reference" == ./* || "$reference" == '$/'* ]] && continue
15	  if [[ "$reference" == docker://* ]]; then
16	    valid='^docker://[^@[:space:]]+@sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$'
17	  else
18	    valid='^[^@[:space:]]+@[0-9a-f]{40}$'
19	  fi
20	  if [[ ! "$reference" =~ $valid ]]; then
21	    printf 'mutable or malformed external action reference: %s\n' "$line" >&2
22	    status=1
23	  fi
24	done < <(rg --no-heading --glob '*.yml' --glob '*.yaml' '^\s*uses:\s*' .github)
25	codeowners=.github/CODEOWNERS
26	if [[ ! -f "$codeowners" ]] \
27	  || ! rg -q '^/\.github/workflows/\s+@[^[:space:]]+$' "$codeowners" \
28	  || ! rg -q '^/\.github/actions/\s+@[^[:space:]]+$' "$codeowners"; then
29	  printf 'CODEOWNERS must cover .github/workflows/ and .github/actions/ with a real owner\n' >&2
30	  status=1
31	fi
32	exit "$status"

880	/// A shell `case` pattern (`key:--flag|key:--flag`) for every flag of `tool`'s shapes.
881	fn flag_patterns(tool: &str) -> String {
882	    let patterns: Vec<String> = TOOL_SHAPES
883	        .iter()
884	        .filter(|shape| shape.tool == tool)
885	        .flat_map(|shape| {
886	            let key = shape.subcommand.join("-");
887	            shape.flags.iter().map(move |flag| format!("{key}:{flag}"))
888	        })
889	        .collect();
890	    if patterns.is_empty() {
891	        "__none__".to_owned()
892	    } else {
893	        patterns.join("|")
894	    }

897	/// The one fake `cargo`, modelling the two subcommands the release path emits.
898	///
899	/// `publish` records the published version under
900	/// `$CALLISTO_TEST_CARGO_MARKER.<crate>`; `info` answers from exactly that
901	/// file, in the real `cargo info` output shapes (exit 0 with a `version:` line,
902	/// or exit 101 with cargo's "could not find" or "failed to load source" text).
903	///
904	/// Invoked without `--registry` it does what real cargo does -- answers from
905	/// the local manifest, the D01 defect -- rather than refusing, so dropping
906	/// `--registry` from the production argv breaks the end-to-end suite instead of
907	/// being absorbed by a lenient fake.
908	///
909	/// `$CALLISTO_TEST_CARGO_MARKER`'s directory also holds the two knobs the
910	/// fakes cannot receive in memory: `unreachable` forces the transport-failure
911	/// shape, and `flap` (`<honest> <absent>` counters) makes a published version
912	/// read as absent for a while, which is index-propagation lag.
913	fn rig_cargo() -> String {
914	    let patterns = flag_patterns("cargo");
915	    format!(
916	        r#"#!/bin/sh
917	printf 'cargo %s\n' "$*" >> "$CALLISTO_TEST_LOG"
918	if [ -n "$CALLISTO_TEST_CARGO_CALLS" ]; then
919	  printf '%s|%s\n' "$PWD" "$*" >> "$CALLISTO_TEST_CARGO_CALLS"
920	fi
921	# Real cargo takes global `--config KEY=VALUE` before the subcommand.
922	while [ "$1" = "--config" ]; do shift 2; done
923	case "$1" in
924	  publish|info) key=$1 ;;

content.text:
Five of the findings from this round now have PRs, and the rest of the list is still open. Nothing has run in GitHub CI yet, and everything else was checked locally.

## Fixed (draft PRs)
- **#445, macOS runner:** now `macos-latest` in `callisto-ci.yml` and `callisto-release.yml`, as you asked. I had picked `macos-15` without confirming, which was wrong. If you want a pinned label for reproducible release builds, say so.
- **#446, E170:** the generated matrix workflow now checks out `ref: ${{ github.sha }}` in `plan`, `build-python` and `execute`. I reproduced E170 on the real binary first. The golden snapshot changes by three lines, the init test now pins those three checkouts, and a CLI test documents the attached-HEAD failure. I haven't run the generated file on a real GitHub runner. Please tell monokl: an existing workflow needs `ref: ${{ github.sha }}` on those three checkouts.
- **#447, attestation:** the installer and the CI job now pass `--source-ref refs/heads/main`.
  - **Tested on real assets:** the pin verifies releases 0.10.0 to 0.17.0 with `gh` 2.103.3, a wrong ref fails, and `--signer-ref` doesn't exist.
  - **Stub:** it now rejects flags the real `gh` lacks, and swapping in `--signer-ref` fails 10 installer tests.
  - **CI job:** it gains a wrong-ref negative control.
- **#448, pins:** the pin checker now scans the templates and fails when one action resolves to two commits. It failed on exactly the three known drifts before the fix, and those pins are now aligned.
- **#449, cargo registry:** a provider test now asserts a custom registry reaches the publish argv, and it fails when the flag is dropped. The fake `cargo` also records which registry a publish landed in. No e2e fixture uses a custom cargo registry yet, so the provider test is the only guard today.

## Corrections to my earlier analysis
- **pypi observation auth:** not a defect. `docs/publishing.md:135` already documents it as a limitation, so I left it alone.
- **"Released N package(s)":** the spec fixes that wording (`REL-CMD-11`), so changing it is your call.
- **Fake `cargo publish` ignoring `--registry`:** only true for a custom registry. The crates.io default correctly sends no flag.

## Still open from this round
1. Installer silently falls back to `cargo install` on any download failure, which bypasses `verification=require`.
2. Unpinned dev tools in the release `verify` job.
3. Three diverged `RELEASE_CREDENTIALS` lists.
4. Substring matching in the rate-limit and auth detectors.
5. The tag probe turning "could not check" into "nothing missing".
6. The receipt not distinguishing "adopted" from "published" when the race happens at publish time.

The backlog from before also remains, so the "fix all findings" ask is not met yet:
- Cargo `url` is accepted but ignored.
- Yarn drops `--registry`.
- Root `Cargo.toml` loses its BOM and gets mixed line endings.
- Dispatch skips `verify`.
- Late npm publishes get almost no confirmation window.
- Pre-mode can plan a lower or already-released prerelease.
- The E320 `.all()` misalignment.
- The changelog already-written check and the `overrides` rewrite.
- The E167 interrupted upload.
- The release-commit path check being looser than its comment.
- The cleanup trails #194 to #199.

The analysis file `.claude/plans/ANALYSIS-2026-11-review-and-slop-patterns.md` still shows the old status for the items fixed above. I'll update it when I do the next batch.

Your side: the Entire gates, merging #445 first, then updating the other PRs so CI reruns, and resolving the old findings in Entire.

Shall I continue down the open list in the order above?

content.text:
Yes, the last several PRs were one-off fixes, and I'm not opening any more until we've agreed the plan below.

PR #450 (draft) now puts `main` on `macos-latest`, since #445 merged with `macos-15`. It's open and nothing has run on it yet.

## What went wrong
- **Instances, not families:** #446 to #450 each fix one site. The runner label alone shows it. It's in four places (CI preflight, release build, the CI test matrix, `matrix.rs`), plus the generated template's pins. I changed it from `macos-14` to `macos-15` to `macos-latest` without once asking what you wanted, and nothing yet checks that any of those labels still exists.
- **No check of intent:** I assumed your "pin latest" meant a specific version instead of asking.
- **Process breaches:** pushing to a merged branch and editing a merged PR's text. #445's title now says `macos-latest` but it merged `macos-15`.
- **Inconsistent verification:** some PRs got a real-tool check or a mutation test (#447, #449) and others only local tests.

## What doing it holistically looks like
Fix each family once, with a guard, so the whole class can't come back:

1. **Pins and labels (one owner):** a single source for runner labels and action pins, a check that runs on `.tmpl` files, and a scheduled job that confirms every label still resolves. #450 and #448 would fold into this.
2. **Fakes vs real tools:** the argument grammar of each fake (`git`, `gh`, `cargo`, `npm`) validated against the real tool. #447's flag allowlist, #449's registry tagging and the git refspec fix are all instances of this.
3. **Generated output as the downstream repo sees it:** a test that renders the workflow and runs it the way a downstream repo does. #446 is one instance.
4. **Verification parity:** one command equal to CI, and a worker report naming the proving command for each claim.
5. **Silent fallbacks and sibling paths:** a systematic pass over all of them, with a ratchet. This is the Rust sweep, with a separate verifier agent on each hit.

## Proposed next steps
I'd merge the open PRs that are already right (#446, #447, #448, #449, #450), run the five family fixes as five scoped efforts, and stop filing single-site PRs.

Before I start: should runner labels be `macos-latest` everywhere, including the release build, or pinned for reproducible release builds? That is the one decision that decides how many places change.

CI is still running on every PR (nothing red, most still pending), so this order is a recommendation to confirm as checks go green. All pairs are conflict-free, so the order below is about risk, not conflicts.

## Merge order
1. **#442, tag push refspec.** Rust-only, includes the fix for the high harness finding, and it already has 8 checks passing. It fixes a real bug (an ambiguous tag push).
2. **#449, cargo registry guard.** Test-only, no behavior change.
3. **#446, E170 in the matrix template.** Merge it before #448, because both change the matrix snapshot.
4. **#448, one commit per action.** After #446 lands, update it from `main` and let CI rerun before merging. The two snapshot edits are on different lines, so they should combine cleanly, but only CI on the combined result proves it.
5. **#447, attestation `--source-ref`.** Merge after its `Release Asset Attestation` job passes on the PR. That job runs the new wrong-ref negative control against the real latest release, which is the only live test of it.
6. **#431, release PR hold note.** Last of the group. It is the biggest change (8 commits) and the only one that edits release automation. Merge it when no release is in flight.
7. **#432, the release PR.** After everything above is in, it will regenerate on the next push to `main`. Review its rendered changelog, then merge it, and watch the first real run: that is also the first release to build on `macos-latest`.

Notes:
- Each merge makes the others "behind". If the repo requires up-to-date branches, update each before merging; I can do that.
- Each PR still needs your Entire Gates approval. #442 also has two findings I fixed that show open until you resolve them.
- If a macOS job fails with "not acquired by Runner", that's capacity. Rerun it.

## Cleanup
Safe to delete (merged, remote gone):
- **Local branches:** `fix/contract-null-branch-and-matcher`, `fix/error-envelope`, `fix/npm-observation-credentials`, `fix/publish-classifier-success-first`, `fix/release-preview-preconditions`, `fix/spec-drift-2026-11`, `test/release-pending-contract`, `test/review-followups`, `test/spec-assertion-gaps`, `ci/macos-latest-runners`, `worktree-entire-hooks-update`.

- **Leave alone:** `slopfix/*` belong to another job, and `macos-15-runners` is this session's worktree.

# Stability

What Callisto promises to keep working from 1.0, and what it does not. A breaking change to anything in the first table needs a major version.

## Stable

| Surface | The promise |
| --- | --- |
| The eight commands (`add`, `status`, `version`, `pre`, `snapshot`, `init`, `release`, `completions`) and their flags | A flag keeps its meaning; a new flag never changes what the command did without it. |
| Exit codes | `0` success, `1` failure, `2` usage error. |
| `--format json` reports | Every report carries `schemaVersion`. Within a version a field is not removed, renamed or retyped; fields may be added. A shape change bumps the version. |
| `callisto.toml` | A key keeps its meaning. Unknown keys are an error, so a new key arrives in a minor release and never changes an existing file's behavior. |
| Changesets | The `.changeset/*.md` format and `pre.json` stay compatible with `@changesets/cli` for npm names; other ecosystems use `ecosystem/name` keys. |
| Error codes | A code keeps naming the same condition and is never reused. New codes may appear. |
| Tag names | `{name}@{version}` by default, `ecosystem/name@{version}` once another ecosystem has a package of that name. Pin a name with `tag-template` if a stable tag matters to your tooling. |
| The GitHub Actions | The inputs of `callisto-action` and `setup-callisto`. The floating `v1` tag moves only on stable releases; pin a commit for a fixed version. |

## CI plumbing

The generated workflows use `release plan`, `release inspect`, `release execute`, `release artifact-manifest`, `release build-python`, `release-pr`, `matrix`, `compose-pr-body` and `schema`. They are hidden from `--help` and work 

## Not covered

- Text output, stderr, warnings and the wording of error messages.
- The library crates (`callisto-model`, `-manifests`, `-graph`). They are internal and version in lockstep with the CLI.
- The order of keys in JSON output, and timing or performance.
- Platforms without a published binary. Windows is not supported.

The `slopfix` worktrees hold nothing that needs saving as code, but there are five learnings worth passing to the plugins session. The dead-code and narration audits both finished, and I've changed nothing on `main` yet.

## What's in the `slopfix` worktrees
They belong to the finished wisp-plugins slop-evaluation job. Each applies the Entire reviewer's slop findings on a Callisto PR. The number is the Entire change: `callisto/40` is the hold-note PR #431, and the others are `42`, `43`, `44` and `46`.
- **42, 43 (committed):** already in `main`. 42 deduplicates the pending-contract test fixture onto the shared harness. 43 moves the problem-matcher test into the Test job.
- **44, 46:** two reworded changesets ("lead with what users see"). The committed parts are in `main`, and only the rewording is uncommitted.
- **40:** uncommitted slop fixes on the hold-note scripts, with **unresolved merge-conflict markers in `justfile`** (`<<<<<<< HEAD`). It isn't a usable state.

## Learnings for the plugins session
1. **Slop deletion can remove a real guard.** Slopfix 40 deletes `run_is_newest` and the "skipped" outcome as over-engineering. `run_is_newest` was added to fix a genuine review finding: a delayed rebuild overwriting a newer hold note. A fixer should check why code exists (`git log -S`, earlier findings) before deleting it.
2. **Fixers must merge `main` and re-verify.** Slopfix 40 forked from a stale base and was left with conflict markers.
3. **CI placement matters.** A test that builds the CLI belongs where there's a Rust toolchain (slopfix 43).
4. **Test dedupe:** prefer the shared harness over a local copy (slopfix 42).
5. **Changeset style:** open with what users see, not the internal change.

**A problem worth your attention:** the 42 and 43 commits carry `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/...` trailers, and they are already in `main` on the public repo. That breaks your "no session links" rule. I can't undo it without rewriting `main`, so the plugins session should stop adding the trailer.

## Dead code (checked: my reference counts match the agent's)
- **Dead, no references beyond the definition (items 1, 2, 6, 10 in the agent's report):**
  - the legacy publish wire types in `plan.rs`;
  - the unused registry traits, `kind_str` and `RegistryError::Network`;
  - four error variants that are never built (E248, E253, E008, E050);
  - seven public methods with no callers, and `derive_unreleased_decision`.
- **Dead apart from their own tests (items 3 to 5, 7 to 9):**
  - the whole pre-cursor family, with errors E257/E258;
  - the write-only plan fields `pre_cursor_updates` and `observed_versions`, and `CascadeOutcome.iterations`;
  - two unused parameters, and an `allow(unused_imports)` that should be `#[cfg(test)]`.
- **Files and tasks:** `assets/callisto-logo-2.*` (477 KB) is unreferenced. Three `.moon` tasks are probably unused.
- **Clean:** no unused dependencies, E-code registry and docs in sync (268 each), no accepted-but-ignored flags.
- **Semver:** removing public items in `callisto-model`, `-graph` or `-manifests` needs a **minor** changeset, or `check-api` fails on the release PR. `docs/stability.md` calls those crates internal.

## Narration and docs: wrong text found
- **Wrong advice:** `napi.rs:108,140` tells users to run `callisto init`, which fails when `callisto.toml` exists. This rests on the error variant and spec, not a run.
- **Wrong or stale prose:**
  - orphaned doc lines at `bump.rs:512`;
  - the `docs/config.md` example shows 4 group members where the real file has 5;
  - ADR 0001 cites E048, which doesn't exist;
  - `docs/releasing.md` says "retried up to four times", but it is three retries;

  - a flag's help text says "this function".

content.text:
Two answers: why #432 fails, then whether the proposed removals touch future work.

## Why the release PR fails
Not a code bug. It is the `check-api` job (`Dependency & API Hygiene`), and Entire Gates also fails because it wants your approval. The release branch itself is current with `main`.

- **The cause:** the release PR computes version **0.17.1**, because all 14 pending changesets are `patch`. Two public API breaks landed since 0.17.0, and under 0.x semver those need a minor bump:
  - `callisto_cli::format_error_json` gained a parameter (from the error-envelope fix, changeset `error-envelope-command.md`).
  - `GraphError::PreJsonRead` gained a `path` field (from the spec-drift fix, changeset `pre-json-read-path.md`).
- **The fix:** raise one of those changesets to `minor`, which makes the release 0.18.0 and passes `check-api`. I'd change `error-envelope-command.md`, since failing commands now print a different JSON error shape on stderr, so it is user-visible. The dead-code removal would also have needed a minor bump, so they can go out together.
- **Your call:** 0.17.1 vs 0.18.0 is a version decision. Say go and I'll open the one-line PR. Merging it triggers the usual hold-then-refresh cycle on #432.

## Does anything proposed for removal matter for future features or languages?
Mostly no, with a few things I'd hold back.

- **Checked:** no doc, spec, ADR, plan or roadmap mentions any removal candidate (I searched `docs/`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, the README and the local plans). `ROAD-TO-V1.md` says Go and NuGet are "architecture examples only", with co-located Cargo/Maturin after v1.
- **How a new language is added:** a new `Ecosystem` variant (`Go`, `Maven`, `NuGet`, `Deno` and `Jsr` already exist, "demand-gated") plus a `RegistryEcosystem` adapter. `adapter_for` returns "unsupported" for everything except cargo, npm and pypi today. None of the removal candidates is part of that path.
- **Safe to remove for that reason:** the old registry traits (`RegistryClient`, `RateLimitPolicy`, `TimeProvider`) belonged to the deleted orchestrator, and the current adapters have their own retry policy. The legacy `plan-publish` wire types and the pre-cursor family also belong to removed or unused designs.
- **Hold back or decide:**
  - The `DiagnosticCode` variants marked "kept for wire compatibility": keep.
  - `go_mod_sample` in the fixtures corpus: it's the only item tied to Go, so keep it.
  - Unused helpers like `is_dual_published`, `platform_manifests` and `GroupTable::try_from_groups`: the concept is live (napi and maturin platform packages), only the helper is unused. I'd keep them until the Cargo/Maturin work after v1 is scoped.
- **Not read:** I haven't read the whole of `ROAD-TO-V1.md` or the local `NEXT-WORK.md` plan in full, only searched them. If you know of a planned feature near any of these, tell me before the removal PR.

Yes, and I hadn't done this check until you asked. Cleanups and tweaks need to stay consistent with the architecture and spec docs, or those docs need updating alongside. The Hygiene failure is fixed in PR #451 (draft), which raises the release to a minor bump. It has not been merged, and `check-api` still needs to pass on the regenerated release PR.

## What counts as the architecture and semantic model
- **No machine-readable model:** there is no `model.json`. The model was folded into prose in September.
- **What stands in for it:** `ARCHITECTURE.md`, five docs in `docs/architecture/`, the 12 ADRs, `docs/specs/*.json` (tests pin these) and two enforcement tests. Those tests are `architecture.rs`, which guards against hand-parsing manifests, and `error_registry_architecture.rs`, which checks the E-code registry.

## Proposed removals vs those docs
- **Consistent:** no architecture doc, spec or ADR mentions any dead-code candidate (plan wire types, registry traits, pre-cursor, the dead error variants, the unused methods).
- **Needs doc and test edits with it:**
  - removing a variant means deleting its row from `docs/errors.md`, which the registry test pins at 268 rows;
  - removing E-codes should be noted in `wire-compat.md` or `stability.md`, since "a code is never reused";
  - `ARCHITECTURE.md` should lose any module description for removed code.

## This session's changes vs those docs (some are now out of date)
- **Attestation:** `architecture/release.md:139` says binaries are checked against the repo and signer. It needs "and `--source-ref refs/heads/main`" (PR #447).
- **Generated workflow:** `cli.json:306` lists the matrix jobs but doesn't say `plan`, `build-python` and `execute` check out the release commit. `release.json:164` already says plan and execute need a detached HEAD, so the product matches its spec and only the generated-workflow spec lags (PR #446).
- **Action pins:** no doc states "one commit per action, templates included", and the pin checker's new rule has no home (PR #448). It belongs in CONTRIBUTING or the architecture release doc.
- **API gate:** `check-api` running only on the release PR isn't documented anywhere either.
- **Consistent already:**
  - runner labels (`matrix.json` says `macos-latest`);
  - the hold workflow (REL-PR specs, which I updated earlier);
  - error envelope fields (`release.md:121`).

## The `check-api` gap
Two public API breaks sat unseen for days and only surfaced on the release PR. Options, smallest first:
1. Run `cargo semver-checks` on every PR as non-blocking, and report breaking changes in the PR checks.
2. Make it blocking on PRs unless a `minor` changeset is present.
3. Keep it release-only.

I'd start with option 1.

## Proposed sequence
1. #451 merges first, so the release can be 0.18.0.
2. Dead-code PR, with the docs/errors edits and a minor changeset.
3. A docs-alignment PR covering attestation, the generated-workflow spec, the pin rule and the narration fixes, plus the `check-api` change.

Shall I proceed with 2 and 3, or do you want to choose among the `check-api` options first?

write(p, s)
print("done")

import re

def cut_variant(path, field_line_regex):
    s = open(path).read()
    m = re.search(field_line_regex, s, flags=re.M)
    assert m, (path, field_line_regex)
    line_start = s.rfind("\n", 0, m.start()) + 1
    # walk back to the start of the attribute block: first preceding line that is blank or a brace/other variant end
    lines = s[:line_start].split("\n")
    # lines[-1] is "" (before line_start); drop preceding attribute lines (#[error..], #[diagnostic..], doc comments) until a blank line
    i = len(lines) - 1
    while i > 0 and lines[i - 1].strip() != "" and not lines[i - 1].strip().endswith("{") :
        i -= 1
    head = "\n".join(lines[:i])
    line_end = s.index("\n", m.start()) + 1
    tail = s[line_end:]
    if tail.startswith("\n"):
        tail = tail[1:]
    open(path, "w").write(head + ("\n" if head and not head.endswith("\n") else "") + tail)

cut_variant("crates/callisto-graph/src/error.rs", r"^\s*UnknownRegistry \{ key: String \},$")

cut_variant("crates/callisto-model/src/vcs/mod.rs", r"^\s*RepoNotFound \{ path: PathBuf, message: String \},$")

p = "docs/errors.md"
s = open(p).read()
s = "".join(l for l in s.splitlines(True) if not any(l.startswith(f"| {c} |") for c in ("E253", "E008", "E050")))
open(p, "w").write(s)
print("ok")

import re, sys

def remove_fn(path, name):
    s = open(path).read()
    m = re.search(rf"^([ \t]*)(pub(\([a-z]+\))? )?(const )?fn {re.escape(name)}\b", s, flags=re.M)
    assert m, (path, name)
    indent = m.group(1)
    start = m.start()
    # include preceding doc comments / attributes
    lines_before = s[:start].split("\n")
    k = len(lines_before) - 1  # index of the (empty) tail piece
    j = k
    while j > 0:
        prev = lines_before[j - 1].strip()
        if prev.startswith("///") or prev.startswith("#[") or prev.startswith("//"):
            j -= 1
        else:
            break
    start = len("\n".join(lines_before[:j])) + (1 if j > 0 else 0)
    # find body end by brace matching from the first '{' after the signature
    brace = s.index("{", m.end())
    depth = 0
    i = brace
    in_str = False
    in_char = False
    while i < len(s):
        c = s[i]
        if in_str:
            if c == "\\":
                i += 1
            elif c == '"':
                in_str = False
        else:
            if c == '"':
                in_str = True
            elif c == "'" and s[i + 2:i + 3] == "'" :
                i += 2
            elif c == "{":
                depth += 1
            elif c == "}":
                depth -= 1
                if depth == 0:
                    break
        i += 1
    end = s.index("\n", i) + 1
    if s[end:end + 1] == "\n":
        end += 1
    removed = s[start:end]
    open(path, "w").write(s[:start] + s[end:])
    print(f"--- removed {name} from {path} ({removed.count(chr(10))} lines)")

One registry: every diagnostic code is a numeric `E####`, across every crate (`callisto-model`, `callisto-graph`, `callisto-cli`). `callisto-cli`'s `CliError` also has variants that wrap another crate's error transparent

"Fix" is the code's `help(...)` text verbatim. "—" means the variant has no help text in the source.

Removes code and files with no live purpose, found by a read-only sweep and then checked here. A public function counted as dead only if the definition was its sole reference in code, docs, specs and plans; `rg -w` per name and `git log -S` showed the thing it served was already gone.

- **Legacy `plan-publish` wire types** in `callisto-model/plan.rs`, and the registry client traits (`RegistryClient`, `RateLimitPolicy`, `TimeProvider`), `kind_str` and `RegistryError::Network`, left behind by the removed orchestrator.
- **The pre-cursor family**: `conventional/pre_cursor.rs`, E257 and E258, `TagIndex::pre_cursor`, the write-only `VersionPlan.pre_cursor_updates` and `observed_versions` (not serialized), and `CascadeOutcome.iterations`.
- **Error variants nothing constructs**: E008, E050, E253. E253's condition already fails as E254, and the other two are covered by other coded paths. `docs/errors.md` drops their rows and lists the codes as retired.
- **Eight public functions with no callers**: `same_content_at`, `paths_changed_since`, `resolve_pre_state`, `display_form`, `linked_group_of`, `into_evidence`, `Changeset::to_markdown`, `derive_unreleased_decision` (a thin wrapper over `derive_release_roster`, which stays).
- **Two unused parameters** (`pre_mutation_checks`, `ManifestWalkResolver::build`) with the test stand-in that existed to fill one, and a blanket `allow(unused_imports)` in `walk.rs`.
- **`assets/callisto-logo-2.*`**, unreferenced.

Left alone on purpose: E248 (`WorkspaceVersionConflict`), because `docs/architecture/versioning.md` says shared `[workspace.package]` writes are unconditional, so it may be a missing check and not dead code (tracked separately); the `DiagnosticCode` variants documented as kept for wire compatibility; helpers only tests call; and `go_mod_sample`, which belongs to the demand-gated Go ecosystem.

No architecture doc, ADR or spec mentions any removed item. Removing public items in the internal crates needs a minor release, so this carries a `minor` changeset (the release is already 0.18.0 through #451).

Checked: `cargo check`, clippy with `-D warnings`, `cargo doc` with warnings denied, and the full workspace test run (86 suites, 2,373 tests, none failed). Not checked: `cargo semver-checks`, which runs only on the release PR.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Fails when the public API changed more than the pending changesets allow.
# A feature PR has not bumped the version yet, so the release type comes from the pending changesets; the release PR
# has consumed them and its bumped version decides.
set -euo pipefail

root=${CHECK_API_ROOT:-$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)}
cd "$root"

level=''
shopt -s nullglob
for file in .changeset/*.md; do
  [[ $file == */README.md ]] && continue
  while IFS= read -r bump; do
    case $bump in
      major) level=major ;;
      minor) [[ $level == major ]] || level=minor ;;
      patch) [[ -n $level ]] || level=patch ;;
    esac
  done < <(sed -n '1,/^---$/!{/^---$/q;p;}' "$file" | sed -n 's/^[^:]*: *\(major\|minor\|patch\) *$/\1/p')
done

if [[ -z $level ]]; then
  cargo semver-checks check-release
  exit
fi

# Before 1.0 a minor release may break the API and a patch release may only add to it, which cargo-semver-checks names one step up.
major_version=$(sed -n 's/^version = "\([0-9]*\)\..*/\1/p' crates/callisto-cli/Cargo.toml | head -n1)
release_type=$level
if [[ $major_version == 0 ]]; then
  case $level in
    patch) release_type=minor ;;
    minor | major) release_type=major ;;
  esac
fi
echo "pending changesets allow a $level release; checking the API as a $release_type change"
cargo semver-checks check-release --release-type "$release_type"

script=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)/scripts/check-api.sh

trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
mkdir -p "$work/bin"
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho "cargo $*" >> "$CALLS"\n' > "$work/bin/cargo"
chmod +x "$work/bin/cargo"

fail=0
# usage: expect <name> <crate version> <expected cargo args> [changeset...]; each changeset is "name:level".
expect() {

- **How it works:** `.github/scripts/check-api.sh` reads the highest bump in the pending `.changeset/*.md` files and passes it to `cargo semver-checks` as `--release-type`. Before 1.0 it shifts one step up, because a patch release may only add to the API and a minor release may break it. With no pending changesets, as on the release PR, the bumped version decides, as before.
- **What it catches:** a PR that breaks the API without announcing a `minor` fails with the same two errors #432 showed, now at PR time.
- **Checked on the real tool:** with a `minor` pending, the script passes. Forcing `minor` reproduces the two failures from the release PR (the extra `format_error_json` parameter and the `PreJsonRead` field).
- **Tests:** seven stub cases cover the 0.x and 1.x mapping, and swapping the 0.x mapping fails two of them. shellcheck, zizmor and the workflow policy check pass. actionlint shows only the known `$/` self-reference. The CI job itself hasn't run yet.
- **Cost and gap:** about three minutes added to the Hygiene job on every PR. `just ci` still doesn't run `check-api` because it needs the network and the published crates. That is the local-versus-CI parity gap from earlier, and CONTRIBUTING now says so. I could add `machete`, `features-boundary` and `check-api` to a separate `just ci-full` recipe as a follow-up.

#452 (dead code, minor changeset) will be the first PR this affects. It should pass, because it carries its own `minor`.

Next on my list is the docs and specs alignment PR, unless you want the E248 investigation first. E248 is the possible missing check on shared workspace versions, and it could be a real silent-wrong-version bug.

content.text:
Yes, mostly. The failure it guards against was loud, caught before shipping, and cost one one-line PR (#451). In exchange I added a 40-line bash parser for changeset frontmatter, a 0.x release-type mapping that's easy to get wrong, a 7-case stub test, a new way for PRs to go red, and three minutes of CI on every PR.

That breaks your own rules: measure the value before building it, and keep the pipeline lean. It also repeats the trap I named earlier, which is adding a guard for every miss. A guard earns its place when the failure is silent or costly. This one wasn't either.

My recommendation is to close #453 and change nothing else in CI. The release PR check already stops a bad release, and that's the right place for it. If you want one small thing, add a single line to CONTRIBUTING: "a change that breaks a public Rust item needs a `minor` changeset". That is free and needs no script.

I'd also apply the same test to the rest of the cleanup plan:
- **Docs and specs alignment:** keep it. It fixes text that is wrong today, so there's no new machinery.
- **Narration cleanup:** keep the edits to the wrong or misleading comments. The grep guard with ratchets is the same trap, so I'd keep only the zero-false-positive patterns (banners, spec IDs, TODO), or none.
- **E248 investigation:** worth doing, because it might be a silent wrong-version bug, which is the kind of failure that does justify effort.

Shall I close #453, and add the one CONTRIBUTING line to the docs PR?

#!/bin/sh
cd /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/worktrees/macos-15-runners || exit 2
echo "## shell scripts by directory (lines)"
for d in .github/scripts .github/actions .github/tests .github/workflows; do
  n=$(find "$d" -name '*.sh' -type f | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
  l=$(find "$d" -name '*.sh' -type f -exec cat {} + 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
  echo "$d: $n files, $l lines"
done
echo "## product scripts (non-test) with size"
find .github/scripts .github/actions -name '*.sh' -type f -not -path '*/tests/*' -exec wc -l {} + | sort -rn | head -12
echo "## test scripts with size"
find .github/tests .github/actions -path '*tests*' -name '*.sh' -type f -exec wc -l {} + | sort -rn | head -14
echo "## run: blocks in workflows (lines of inline shell)"
for f in .github/workflows/*.yml; do
  n=$(awk '/run: *\|/ {inrun=1; next} inrun && /^ *- |^ {0,6}[a-z-]+:/ {inrun=0} inrun {c++} END {print c+0}' "$f")
  echo "$f: ~$n inline lines"
done
echo "## jq invocations"
grep -rho "jq [^|]*" .github --include=*.sh --include=*.yml 2>/dev/null | wc -l
echo "## already-in-Rust equivalents (release-pr subcommands)"

content.text:
You're right, and the numbers back it up. The shell is small but the testing around it is heavy, and most of this session's bugs were in it.

**Measured (3,609 shell lines against 117,530 lines of Rust):**
- **Product shell:** about 760 lines. The biggest are `create-or-update-release-pr.sh` (245) and `install-callisto.sh` (197). There are also about 160 inline lines in the workflows (115 in `callisto-release.yml`) and 83 `jq` calls.
- **Shell tests:** about 2,650 lines, 3.5 times the code they test. One contract test alone is 615 lines, built from stubbed `gh`, `git` and `cargo`.
- **Bugs this session that were shell-specific:** the `gh_retry` recursion (mine), `jq -e` vs `-r`, `set -e` lost through command substitution, bash 3.2 vs 5 (no associative arrays), BSD vs GNU `sed`, and fakes that accepted flags the real tool rejects (`--signer-ref`).

**Why it's brittle:** the release-PR flow's policy already lives in Rust (`release-pr verify`, `decide` and `commit-plan`). The shell keeps the part that is hardest to test, which is orchestrating `gh`, retries and API calls. We then wrote stub-heavy tests to compensate, and your memory notes say fake-tool tests are exactly what hid the 0.10.1 `gh` regression.

**What I'd do, in order of value:**
1. **Delete the release-PR note feature from #431.** That is `release-pr-note.sh`, `note-release-pr-rebuild.sh`, their tests and the `release-pr-note` job, roughly 300 lines. The draft-hold already prevents the stale merge, and the notes are only explanatory comments. It's the clearest case of polish on top of a guard.
2. **Prune the stub-heavy tests.** Keep the ones that run the real binary (`test_release_pr_decide_binary_contract.sh`, `verify-release-workflow-*`). Drop or shrink the stub-only contract tests, and don't let a stub accept more than the real tool does.
3. **Trim `install-callisto.sh`.** It handles Windows `.zip` assets although Windows is unsupported, and its crates.io fallback is the code that bypasses `verification=require`.
4. **Only if you want it:** move `create-or-update-release-pr.sh` into a Rust subcommand, so its logic gets Rust unit tests and a real `gh` seam. That is the one change that removes the whole class of problems, but it's a real project, so I'd scope it as a spike first.

What I wouldn't do is add more guards around the shell, including the `check-api` script I just proposed.

Which of these do you want? I'd start with 1 and 2, and I won't touch the scripts until you say.

# create/update policy belongs to `callisto release-pr decide`.
#
# The managed branch is never pushed with the Git wire protocol: on a public
# repository, GITHUB_TOKEN cannot write `.github/workflows/*` that way, nor
# through createCommitOnBranch's own fileChanges, on any ref (confirmed

# deterministic staging branch rooted at the current base commit -- which
# never needs to touch `.github/workflows/*`, since that path is inherited
# unchanged from the base -- and only then is the managed branch's ref moved
# onto that commit. A ref move is not itself a write to that path.
set -euo pipefail

cd "$INPUT_CWD"

content.text:
Yes, it fits, and the architecture already says so. `docs/architecture/release.md` states: "GitHub Actions schedules jobs, transports artifacts, and injects credentials. Callisto validates… Workflow shell must not reimplement those semantics." The script's own header says the same: it "executes a typed Callisto release-PR decision" and leaves policy to `release-pr decide`. What remains in shell is only the forge I/O, which Rust already does elsewhere: `forge.rs` and `artifact.rs` call `gh` through the same `CommandRunner` seam, with the same retry and tool-shape tests.

## The minimal version
- **One new hidden subcommand**, `callisto release-pr apply`, next to `verify`, `decide` and `commit-plan` (the CI plumbing already named in `stability.md`). It runs the steps the script runs today, in the same order:
  - take the snapshot;
  - stage the commit;
  - move the branch;
  - create or edit the PR;
  - set the draft or ready state.
- **Reuse, don't build:** the existing `CommandRunner`, the existing retry helper, and the existing `ReleasePrDecisionV2` and `ReleasePrCommitPlanV1` types. No new abstractions.
- **The snapshot moves to Rust too.** `wire-compat.md:27` currently notes that the shell builds it with a hard-coded `schemaVersion: 2`, a wire shape owned by the wrong layer.
- **The shell shrinks** from 245 lines to a call plus the `git add -A` step, about 10 lines.
- **Tests:** a recording runner, like the registry provider tests, replaces the 615-line stub contract test. One real-`gh` read-only check compares the Rust snapshot with the shell snapshot on this repo's actual PR.

## What I would not do
- No new error framework: two or three E-codes at most.
- No change to the flow itself (draft-first, staging branch, tip check). It's a port, not a redesign.
- Nothing around the other scripts. `install-callisto.sh` and `move-floating-tag.sh` are small enough to stay.

## Order
1. **Delete the release-PR note feature** from #431 first (about 300 lines including tests). It is polish, and porting it would be wasted work.
2. **Port the release-PR apply.** This is the real project, so I'd start with the read-only snapshot port and the comparison against the shell's output before porting the writes.
3. **Delete the stub contract test and `gh_retry`** once the Rust path is live.

**Risk:** this path produced the E165 incident, and `createCommitOnBranch` and the ref moves can't be exercised locally. The first real test would be on this repo's release PR, so I'd gate the switch behind the action input (shell stays as fallback for one release) and remove the fallback after a clean cycle.

Want me to start with step 1, and scope step 2 as a plan before writing any Rust?

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# create/update policy belongs to `callisto release-pr decide`.
#
# The managed branch is never pushed with the Git wire protocol: on a public
# repository, GITHUB_TOKEN cannot write `.github/workflows/*` that way, nor
# through createCommitOnBranch's own fileChanges, on any ref (confirmed
# directly against this repository). Instead, the generated
# version-bump changes are committed via the forge commit API onto a
# deterministic staging branch rooted at the current base commit -- which
# never needs to touch `.github/workflows/*`, since that path is inherited
# unchanged from the base -- and only then is the managed branch's ref moved
# onto that commit. A ref move is not itself a write to that path.
set -euo pipefail

# both observations; the working tree changes below (git add -A) never
# create a local commit -- the real commit is made remotely, via the forge
# commit API, on the staging branch.
base_commit=$(git rev-parse HEAD)

# print every failed attempt's stderr, and leave other failures (404, 422) to the caller. `gh pr create`

gh_retry() {
  local attempt=1 delay=2 err code
  err=$(mktemp)
  until gh "$@" 2> "$err"; do
    code=$?
    cat "$err" >&2
    if [[ $attempt -ge 4 ]] || ! grep -qiE 'Something went wrong|HTTP 5[0-9]{2}|Bad Gateway|Service Unavailable|Gateway Time|timed? ?out|connection reset|unexpected EOF' "$err"; then
      rm -f "$err"
      return "$code"
    fi
    echo "::warning::gh $1 hit a transient GitHub error (attempt $attempt of 4); retrying in ${delay}s" >&2
    sleep "$delay"
    delay=$((delay * 2))
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    [[ -z "${RETRY_RESET:-}" ]] || "$RETRY_RESET" || true
  done
  cat "$err" >&2
  rm -f "$err"
}

release_pr_snapshot() {
  local raw_prs
