# Agent guide

Rules for AI agents working in this repo.

## Crates

| Crate | License | Depends on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| callisto-model | MIT | none (external: `michi-graph`, MIT) |
| callisto-manifests | FSL-1.1-MIT | model |
| callisto-graph | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests |
| callisto-cli | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests, graph |
| callisto-fixtures | FSL-1.1-MIT | model (dev-only) |

- `callisto-model` (MIT) must never depend on an FSL crate. It depends on `michi-graph` (MIT, no dependencies of its own) for dependency-graph validation and ordering. `just license-boundary` fails if anything it builds with is FSL.
- Check with `grep -H "^license" crates/*/Cargo.toml` after adding or moving a crate.

## Commands

- Full pipeline: `just ci` (includes the 90% coverage gate). `just test`, `just lint`, `just fmt`.
- Performance: `just bench` times `status`, `version --dry-run` and `release --dry-run` over generated workspaces and counts the git processes each starts (`CALLISTO_BENCH_SHAPES=1` lists which). A change that adds a git process per package fails review.
- Scoped iteration: one `cargo test -p <crate>` or `cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets -- -D warnings` at a time.
  - Not `moon run <project>:test`: its per-project fan-out serializes on `target/`'s build lock.
  - Never run cargo builds in parallel.
- Changesets: `callisto add --package cargo/callisto-cli:<bump> --summary "..."` (non-interactive). Target `callisto-cli`: its changelog is the one users read. One changeset per user-visible topic. Lead with what the user sees now; add an action or limit when it matters. Use a short sentence for a simple change, or a short lead and bullets for related details. No internal names, mechanism or filler.
- Never `git checkout -- Cargo.lock` as cleanup. A lockfile diff means investigate, not discard.

## Invariants

1. Safe Rust only: `unsafe_code = "forbid"`.
2. Manifest edits preserve format: `toml_edit` for TOML; JSON changes that only replace string values are written into the original text by span (`json_text`), anything else keeps key order and fingerprinted indentation. No regex or line edits.
3. File writes go through `callisto_model::atomic::atomic_write`.
4. User-facing errors derive `miette::Diagnostic` with a code and a fix.
5. No emojis in docs or code.
6. No cargo features in shipped crates; behaviour is chosen at runtime (#143). The dev-only `callisto-model/test-util` feature is the exception.
7. No `unwrap()` outside tests (`just lint` denies it). An `expect` names the invariant that makes it unreachable.

## Fixing bugs

- Grep for structurally identical code (same algorithm, other file, ecosystem or mode). A sibling with the same defect is in scope now.
- N copies of one logic: unify to one implementation rather than patching each.
- A deliberately deferred sibling gets an explicit record: changeset note, tracked follow-up or code comment.
- A new shared helper migrates every call site in the same change, or the rest are tracked.

## Specs and plans

- Specs (`spec@1`) live in `docs/specs/`, one per area, current behavior only. Change the spec in the same PR as the behavior. No history, rationale or revision notes.
- This repo's release workflow has no GitHub Environment or reviewer gate and only `execute` gets registry secrets (owner policy, enforced by `.github/tests/verify-release-workflow-policy.sh`). Never add one.
- Read `ARCHITECTURE.md` and the matching `docs/architecture/` topic before changing behavior in an area.
- Read `docs/adr/README.md` before changing release flow, Git access, publishing, distribution, platform packages or manifest writes. Reversing an ADR needs a new ADR the owner accepts.
- Plans (`plan@1`) live in `docs/projects/`. Delete a plan once its work ships.
- Code never cites specs: no spec IDs, criterion IDs, section numbers or track names in comments, test names or messages. Describe the behavior instead.
- A requirement the owner didn't state is a judgment call. Get owner confirmation before it gates anything.

## Writing

- Succinct: short sentences, bullets, tables. No backstory, hedging or filler.
- Never hard-wrap Markdown or PR bodies: one line per paragraph.
- Code comments: one short line, only for a non-obvious why. Wrap at 120 columns (`rustfmt.toml`). No history ("used to", "previously"): git records it.
- No claude.ai session links in commits, PRs or files.

  - `style` defaults to flat only so existing literals compile. The configured default is grouped.
  
  **Unverified:** a real release run with a real tag and repository, and tags containing characters that need percent-encoding in the URL.

input.content:
## Summary

The CLI had the same rules restated at several sites: five JSON-input readers, hand-written "refuse `--dry-run`" errors at each output flag, and file flags resolved against the process directory. Review findings on earlier PRs came from that shape. This puts each rule in one place.

- `io::read_json_input` reads `release-pr` inputs (file, inline JSON or `-` for stdin) and fails with E281. `io::read_json_file` reads the `release` subcommands' files and fails with E238. They stay two functions because merging them would change an error code or let `--intent` take inline JSON.
- `io::OutputFile` is built from the path, `--dry-run` and the flag. It refuses `--dry-run` with that flag's existing error before anything is written, can probe the destination up front, and writes only on `commit`. It is `#[must_use]`. `artifact-manifest --out`, `plan --out`, the receipt and `release-pr commit-plan --out` use it. No error code changed.
- A relative path given to the file flags of `release` and `release-pr` (`--intent`, `--receipt`, `--out`, `--artifact-dir`, `--input`, `--artifact-manifest`, `--source-root`) now resolves against `--cwd`, like `git -C`, not the process directory. Decision-file flags stay relative to the workspace root. The architecture doc and a new spec criterion (CLI-PATH-01) say so.
- `tests/output_flags_conformance.rs` enumerates every path-valued argument of `release` and `release-pr` from the clap definition and fails unless each is classified in one table. A new path flag cannot ship unclassified. For each output flag it asserts the `--dry-run` refusal with its code, that an existing file is left untouched, and that a relative path resolves against `--cwd`.

## Verify

- `just pre-push`, `just lint`, `just doc-check` and `just test` exit 0, as do the release PR action and release workflow contract scripts.
- Mutation checks: ignoring `dry_run` in `OutputFile::new` fails the refusal test, and making the path resolver return its input unchanged fails 7 of 9 tests.
- Built binary in a temp repo with a process directory different from `--cwd`: `commit-plan --out` lands under `--cwd`; `--dry-run` gives E282, E217, E216 and E218 for the four output flags and leaves an existing file intact; a bad JSON file gives E238 and bad inline JSON gives E281.

Gaps: `--artifact-manifest`, `execute`'s `--artifact-dir` and `build-python`'s flags are classified in the table but not run end to end. `build-python` still refuses `--dry-run` by hand (E309), since it writes a directory. The `--emit-preview` and `--preview` flags still resolve from the workspace root and move to this rule in a follow-up once the open PRs touching them have merged.

Not run: CI.

Three independent PRs are open, signed, and pairwise conflict-free. Cleanup is done except the items only you can run.

| PR | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **#473** | "Read before merging" callout in the release PR: `Breaking:` and `Action:` markers, and publishable packages whose source changed but that the release leaves out. A breaking marker removes the "backward compatible" claim. |
| **#474** | Changelog sections grouped by Major/Minor/Patch, with a date and compare link; `layout = "flat"` keeps the old format. |
| **#475** | One JSON-input reader per error code, an `OutputFile` that refuses `--dry-run` through each flag's own error, file flags relative to `--cwd`, and a conformance test over every path flag. |

**Verification:** I ran `just pre-push`, `lint`, `doc-check` and `test`, plus both workflow contract scripts, on each branch and judged by exit code. All exit 0. Every commit is signed (`valid`). CI and reviews are pending. Each PR needs a GitHub review.

**What I changed or added while reviewing the agents' work**
- **Layout PR, release notes:** a fixed group's notes would have filed a mate's Minor entry under Patch. I fixed that in `notes.rs` with tests. This repo uses a fixed group, so it would have hit our own releases.
- **Layout PR, compare link:** it would only appear with a `[release]` table. It now falls back to the GitHub `origin` remote.
- **#473:** `version` and `compose-pr-body` now build the preview through one function. A test caught that they had diverged.
- **Mutation checks:** each PR has at least two that fail the right test.

**Known hazard (in #474's description):** `ChangelogStyle` defaults to flat so older code compiles, while the configured default is grouped. New code that builds a `ChangelogInput` must set it.

**Still open**
- **Labels** need #473 merged first, since they read its findings.
- **The preview path rule** (`--emit-preview` and `--preview` relative to `--cwd`) waits for #475.
- **Merge order** doesn't matter for conflicts. I'd go #473, #474, #475.
- **Left for you** (the classifier refused these): ten remote branches that hold unmerged commits (tips recorded in `plans/archive/remote-branch-tips-2026-11-08.txt`), about 14 old directories under `.claude/worktrees/` that git no longer lists, and pulling your `main` checkout.
- **Worktrees now:** four. `agents-verify` is for #473, `changelog-layout` for #474, and `cli-io` for #475, plus your main checkout. I'll remove each as its PR merges.

```

content.content:
- `expand_selection` (group members) and `require_dependencies_selected` (unselected unreleased dependencies) apply to both routes.

## Managed release PR and workflow

Callisto's own [release workflow](../../.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml) reconstructs one `callisto/version-packages` PR from `main` when changesets land. It versions manifests and changelogs; merging the PR consumes the changesets on `main` and authorizes publication.

- The action commits non-workflow changes through `createCommitOnBranch`, then moves the release ref through REST. It does not run a local `git push`. Workflow files remain unchanged, so the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` needs no workflow-write permission.

content.text:
All five findings on #81 and #82 are fixed and resolved, and the answer to your question is that we had partly lost track of the architecture docs. I fixed that part and opened #476.

**Findings, all verified against the code**

On #473 (change #81):
- **Empty plan:** the body returned early, dropped the "changed, not releasing" list, and claimed the workspace was up to date. It now renders the callout and says "no package is queued".
- **Heading marker:** `## Migration` followed directly by `Breaking: …` produced no marker, because the heading stayed as the paragraph's first line. An ATX heading is now a block of its own.
- **Git processes per package:** this was a real violation of `AGENTS.md:23`, which says a change that adds a git process per package fails review. It is a line in the file I edited in #472. Covered packages are now skipped, and only a package that changed by tree id (one batched pass) pays for a file listing. A test shows the cost is identical for 3 and 24 unchanged packages.

On #474 (change #82):
- **Compare link:** a `#` in a tag template ended the URL path. Both refs are now percent-encoded.
- **Fenced group heading:** my group-merge for release notes recognized a heading inside a fenced example. It now uses the shared fence tracker. This is the same "second scanner" mistake we fixed before, in code I added.

Each fix has a test, and each of the five has a mutation check that fails correctly. `just pre-push`, `lint`, `doc-check`, `test` and both workflow contract scripts exit 0 on both branches. All commits are signed, and both PRs are pushed.

**Are we losing track?**
- **Specs and the semantic model:** current. Each PR updated its criteria (REL-PR-04, REL-PR-10, VER-CS-09 and 10, VER-APPLY-07A, CLI-PATH-01) and the `versioning.md` architecture doc.
- **The two documents people read first:** stale. The data flow in `ARCHITECTURE.md` and the release-PR section of `release.md` didn't mention the preview, the PR-body flow, the offline publish plan or the Markdown module. **#476** fixes that for what is on `main` today. The three open PRs add their own lines after they merge.
- **The plan:** `PLAN-release-notes.md` (local, in the main plans folder) is current. The repo's `NEXT-WORK.md` and the artifact page are not, and I haven't touched either.
- **What I didn't do:** I never ran an architecture-conformance check, such as the `scribe` architecture audit, against the model. I worked from the conversation and the docs. That gap is why the drift went unnoticed.

**What I'd add** (say if you want it): a short "docs touched" line in each PR's checklist, naming `ARCHITECTURE.md`, the architecture doc and the spec, so a flow change can't merge without them.

Open PRs are #473, #474, #475 and #476, all independent and needing a review each.

content.text:
The four open PRs work together, with one semantic conflict that I'm handling at merge time. I tested the combination in a scratch worktree rather than assuming it from each PR passing alone.

**The combined test**
- **Textually clean:** #473, #474, #475 and #476 merge together with no conflicts.
- **Compile error found:** #473 added a test that builds a `ChangelogInput` literal, and #474 added a required `style` field. Merged together, the lint and test steps fail with `missing field style`. This is the "defaults to flat" hazard I flagged in #474, showing up in practice.
- **The fix is one line:** adding `style: Default::default(),` to that test literal. With it, the combined tree passes `just pre-push`, `lint`, `doc-check`, `test` and both workflow contract scripts.
- **When to apply it:** it can only go on the PR that merges second, because neither branch has both halves. Merge order is #473 first. Then I merge `main` into #474 and add the line. I've written this into `PLAN-release-notes.md`.

**Real end-to-end run (temp repo, a real tag, a GitHub `origin`)**
- **Changelog:** it shows `## 1.1.0`, then `_2026-11-08 · [compare](…/compare/a@1.0.0...a@1.1.0)_`, then the Minor and Patch groups.
- **PR body, combined binary:** it shows the "Read before merging" callout with the `Breaking:` item, the "Merging will publish" table (`crates.io · git tag`), and no "backward compatible" claim.
- **Without #473** the same run still says "backward compatible" next to a `Breaking:` marker, which is the bug #473 fixes.
- **Still not exercised:** a real GitHub release and a real registry. The publish table is from the offline plan.

**Also this round**
- **Checklist:** the PR template now has a Docs line (on #476).
- **Artifact:** the page has a "Where this stands" section: merged, in review, next, and how it differs from the mock-ups.
- **Scratch worktree:** removed.

**Waiting on you:** a GitHub review on #473, #474, #475 and #476. Labels and the preview path rule start once #473 and #475 merge, since both build on them.

content.text:
Yes, the Release workflow failed on the last two merges to `main`, and I caused it. The fix is open as PR #477 and needs a quick review.

**What failed**
- **Runs:** the Release and CI runs on `69a9329af` and `3625c6f93` both failed. The release run failed at "Verify release candidate" with `error[E0063]: missing field style in initializer of ChangelogInput`.
- **Impact:** that gate failed first, so the artifact build, execute and release PR refresh were skipped. Nothing was published or half-done, and the release PR #468 is simply not refreshed.
- **Not run:** the Release workflow runs on `main` pushes, so I haven't seen it pass since. It will re-run when #477 merges.

**Cause**
- #473 added a test that builds a `ChangelogInput`, and #474 added a required `style` field. Each PR passed alone, and the four merge textually clean.
- I found this exact conflict in my combined test and wrote down that #474 needed the one-line fix after #473 merged. The PRs merged before I applied it, so `main` went red. I should have put the fix on #474 before it could merge, instead of leaving it as a note.

**The fix (#477)**
- **Change:** one line, `style: Default::default()` in the test literal.
- **Checks:** `just pre-push`, `lint`, `doc-check`, `test` and both workflow contract scripts exit 0. The commit is signed.

**A gap this exposed**
- The `main` ruleset lists no required status checks (`required_status_checks: []`), so the merge queue doesn't require CI. PR checks also run once on the PR head, so a PR that goes stale against a moved `main` can merge with an old green.
- Requiring the CI checks in the ruleset would have blocked this. That's your setting to change, and I haven't touched it.

**Next:** once #477 merges, I'll confirm the Release workflow goes green and the release PR refreshes. Labels and the preview path rule come after that.

## Summary

`version --emit-preview` and `compose-pr-body --preview` now resolve a relative path against `--cwd`, like the file flags of `release` and `release-pr` (#475). Only `--emit-decision` stays relative to the workspace root, because it names a committed repository file.

- Both commands use `GlobalArgs::resolve_file_arg`. They no longer read the workspace root for this, so with `--cwd` below the repository root a preview lands under `--cwd` and is read from there.
- The architecture doc, the `CLI-PATH-01` criterion and the flag help say so. Behavior with the default `--cwd` (the current directory at the repository root) is unchanged. The release PR action passes an absolute temporary path, so it is unaffected.
- New test: with `--cwd` set to a subdirectory, `version` writes `preview.json` there and not at the root, and `compose-pr-body` reads it from there. Reverting `version` to the workspace root fails it.

## Verify

`just pre-push`, `just lint`, `just doc-check`, `just test` and the two workflow contract scripts exit 0, with the one-line fix from #477 applied locally (not committed here). Until #477 merges, `main` and this PR's CI fail on a test that does not compile; the two changes are independent and identical where they overlap.

def run(args):

cases = [

        "let breaking = has(FINDING_BREAKING_MARKER) || has(FINDING_MAJOR_BUMP);",

    (
        ".github/actions/callisto-action/scripts/create-or-update-release-pr.sh",
        '      if grep -Fxq -- "$name" <<< "$current_labels"; then edit_args+=(--remove-label "$name"); fi',
        "      :",
        ["bash", ".github/actions/callisto-action/tests/test_release_pr_contract.sh"],
        "Script: stale labels are never removed",
    ),
]
for path, old, new, cmd, label in cases:
    full = repo + path
    original = open(full).read()
    assert original.count(old) == 1, (label, original.count(old))
    backup = os.path.join(tmp, os.path.basename(path) + ".baklabels")
    shutil.copy(full, backup)
    open(full, "w").write(original.replace(old, new))
    # the contract script prints FAIL lines but its exit code is the verdict
    code = run(cmd)
    shutil.copy(backup, full)
    print(f"{label}: exit={code} ({'caught' if code else 'NOT CAUGHT'}), restored={open(full).read() == original}")

## Summary

## Summary

The first real release PR built with the new flow (#468) said **"This release would fail: E169 … `cargo/callisto-fixtures` configures no publish target to dispatch"**. The release is healthy. `callisto-fixtures` is a private member of the fixed group, bumped with its group (0.18.0 released that way). The preview passed every bumped package as an explicit selection to the offline plan, and an explicit selection of a package with no publish target is refused.

- New `publish_outlook_in(ws, preview)` in `callisto-graph` selects the bumped packages that have a publish target and plans those; `compose-pr-body --publish-plan` calls it. Selection and planning are in one function, so the CLI cannot get the selection wrong.
- If no bumped package publishes anywhere, the outlook is an empty plan instead of a failure.

## Verify

- New end-to-end test: a fixed group with a `publish = false` member. The member is bumped, the outlook is a plan listing only the publishable crate. Removing the publishable filter makes the test fail with E169, the same error as on #468.
- `just pre-push`, `just lint`, `just doc-check`, `just test` and the two workflow contract scripts exit 0.

After this merges, the release PR's caution should disappear and "Merging will publish" should list the crates. Not run: CI, or the release PR refresh on GitHub.

 # callisto-cli
 
+## 0.19.0
+
+_2026-11-09 · [compare](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/compare/callisto@0.18.0...callisto@0.19.0)_
+
+### Minor Changes
+
+- Changelog sections are now grouped into Major, Minor and Patch Changes, with the release date and, when the GitHub repository is known (from `[release] forge-repository` or the `origin` remote) and the previous version has a tag, a compare link under the version heading. A fixed group's GitHub release notes keep each member's entries under the bump group they were recorded in. Set `layout = "flat"` under `[changelog]` in `callisto.toml` to keep the old single-list format.
+- The release PR body now has a "Read before merging" callout. It lists each `Breaking:` and `Action:` paragraph from a changeset, and the packages whose source changed since their last release but that the release leaves out. A breaking paragraph removes the "backward compatible" claim.
+- The release PR body now lists where merging will publish each package (registries, git tag, GitHub release, assets), planned from the versioned tree with no registry lookup. If that plan would be refused, the body leads with a caution naming the error. `compose-pr-body --publish-plan` turns it on, and the release PR action passes it.
+- The release PR now carries labels that say what a reader should expect: `callisto: ready`, `blocked`, `breaking`, `action-required` or `unreleased-changes`, plus `bump: major`, `minor` or `patch`. The action creates missing labels and removes ones that stopped applying.
+- `callisto version --emit-preview <path>` writes the facts a release PR body is built from, and `compose-pr-body --preview <path>` renders from that file. The release PR action uses both, so the body can be composed after the changesets are consumed. `--emit-preview` with `--dry-run` fails with E276, as `--emit-decision` does.
+
+### Patch Changes
+
+- The release PR flags a `Breaking:` note on a change whose bump is too low for it: patch or minor from 1.0.0, or patch before.
+- Relative file flags of `release` and `release-pr` now resolve against `--cwd` instead of the process directory.
+- The release PR's package table now labels bare-named packages with their real ecosystem (`cargo`, `npm` or `pypi`) instead of `core`.
+- A change whose first paragraph starts with a code span, a `#hashtag` or a `~` is now titled by that paragraph in the release PR instead of by its changeset file name.
+- The release PR body now groups changes under Major, Minor and Patch headings and titles each change with its first paragraph instead of the changeset file name. A change with nothing beyond its title is a bullet.
+- Headings in a changeset now sit under the release PR's own headings instead of at the level the author wrote. Headings inside code fences are left alone.
+- `version --emit-preview` and `compose-pr-body --preview` now resolve a relative path against `--cwd`, like the other file flags. Only `--emit-decision` stays relative to the workspace root.
+- The release PR no longer says a healthy release "would fail" when a fixed group has a private member. Only packages that publish somewhere are planned for the "Merging will publish" table.

Yes, but only one item is worth doing, and it can wait for the release. I took it from the real 0.19.0 diff, not from guesses.

3. **A pre-1.0 reminder in the "Read before merging" block.** The note about minor bumps below 1.0 already appears, so I'd skip this.

Everything else on the list, renderers, rollups and requiring CI, is larger or your decision, and none of it helps 0.19.0 users directly.

content.text:
The finding on #482 was valid, and it's fixed and resolved on the trail.

- **Bug:** when a fixed group's release owner has only the "Released together with" line, its section now has no headings. `group_release_notes` then took the flat path and dropped each member's Major/Minor/Patch group from the published GitHub release notes.
- **Fix:** if the owner has no entries of its own and a member's entries carry bump groups, the merger now builds a grouped section: date line first, then the members' entries under their own groups. A flat owner, or flat members, behave as before.
- **Checks:**
  - The new test `a_group_only_owner_keeps_its_mates_bump_groups` fails when I disable the fix.
  - Pre-push, lint, doc-check, test and both workflow contract scripts exit 0.
  - The commit (2bc1767) is signed and shows `valid` on GitHub.
  - CI has not run on it yet.
- **Why it went unseen:** my first change tested the renderer alone, not the notes merger that reads its output. In this repo the owner (`callisto-cli`) has changes of its own, so it didn't show on #468.

I haven't started the next improvement. Starting another PR now would stack on #482's pending review, which you asked me to avoid. The remaining candidate is the repeated "Also bumped" line, but it's cosmetic and I'd leave it. The larger items (renderers, rollups, requiring CI) still need your decision.

16:- `ReleasePreview` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/release_preview.rs`) is the serializable, versioned view of a plan for people: packages, merged changes, bystanders and findings. Surfaces such as the PR body render it; they do not recompute from the plan. `version --emit-preview` writes it before apply consumes the changesets, and `compose-pr-body --preview` renders from that file. `ReleasePreview` also carries findings from the changesets (a `Breaking:` or `Action:` marker, a breaking marker whose bump is too low, and no \"backward compatible\" claim when there is a breaking one) and `unreleased`, the publishable packages with source changes since their last tag that the plan does not bump (`version --emit-preview` computes it; a failure to look is a warning). `pr_labels()` derives the managed label catalog, with an `applied` flag per label, from the same findings. `--publish-plan` adds `publish`, the outcome of `plan_workspace_release_offline` on the versioned tree for exactly the packages the preview bumps (the committed decision holds those, not every unreleased package). It never observes a registry or the forge, so the checks that need one (a published version left behind, a name another project owns) are left to the release itself; a refusal becomes a `Stop` finding. Rows are keyed by the qualified release identity, so `cargo/x` and `npm/x` stay apart.

**A: #483.** Each change in the release PR now ends with the pull request that added it, for example `· #475` on a bullet or `Pull request #463` under a change with a body. I ran the built binary on this repo's real history and all 14 pending changes showed the right PR, #463 to #482. The number is read from the merge commits with one `git log`. A change added without a pull request shows none, and so does a repo with no commits. Both commits are signed and show `valid`, the work is on trail 250, and the six local checks pass. CI has not run. I left authors out, because git has no GitHub login to link.

**B: required CI on main (not applied).** The automated release PR #468 shows only one check, so CI does not run on it. If I made CI required, #468 could become unmergeable, and a wrong setting blocks every PR. Three ways forward:
1. **Fix CI triggering first.** Make CI run on the bot-created release PR, then require the checks. This is the safest option.
2. **Require the checks and rely on the merge queue.** The queue runs CI at merge time, but I'm not certain it clears the PR-level requirement for a PR that never ran CI.
3. **Leave it.** You can bypass the rules as the repo owner, so this only matters if a stale-green merge happens again.

I'd do option 1 as its own small PR before touching the ruleset.

**Two mistakes this session**
- **Lost edits.** My "restore the tree" step after a real run wiped my uncommitted edits. Nothing was pushed or committed, so I rebuilt them from this session and committed immediately. From now on real runs happen in a scratch worktree.
- **Missed key.** The unit tests passed with keys like `a.md`, but real changeset ids have no `.md`. Only the real run showed it.

lines: Callisto's own [release workflow](../../.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml) reconstructs one `callisto/version-packages` PR from `main` when changesets land. It versions manifests and changelogs; merging the PR consumes the changesets on `main` and authorizes publication.

-- The action commits non-workflow changes through `createCommitOnBranch`, then moves the release ref through REST. It does not run a local `git push`. Workflow files remain unchanged, so the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` needs no workflow-write permission.

+- The action commits non-workflow changes through `createCommitOnBranch`, then moves the release ref through REST. It does not run a local `git push`. Workflow files remain unchanged, so the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` needs no workflow-write permission. A pull request opened with `GITHUB_TOKEN` starts no workflows, so the release PR gets no CI checks; this repository's release workflow passes the `RELEASE_PR_TOKEN` secret (a PAT or GitHub App token) as `github_token` when it is set, and falls back to `GITHUB_TOKEN` when it is not.
- Commits are GitHub-signed as `github-actions[bot]`. An App or fine-grained token can use another identity.
- Branch protection must require reviews and CI checks. CODEOWNERS alone does not enforce review.

- The PR body is composed after the version command, from the `ReleasePreview` it wrote (`version --emit-preview`), because that command consumes the changesets the body describes. `compose-pr-body --preview --publish-plan` also plans the versioned tree's release offline, so "Merging will publish" names only targets the release derives from the same decision, and a plan the release would refuse leads the body with a caution. Registry-side checks stay with the release. The same report lists the labels Callisto manages (`callisto: ready|blocked|breaking|action-required|unreleased-changes`, `bump: major|minor|patch`) each with an `applied` flag derived from the preview's findings, so the action adds, creates and removes labels without naming any. See [versioning](versioning.md).

content.text:
It failed because of a deliberate security rule, not a fussy check, and the miss was mine. I've closed #484.

**What broke:** `verify-release-workflow-policy.sh` allows only the `execute` job (the one that publishes) to reference secrets. I put `RELEASE_PR_TOKEN` in the `version-pr` job, so it failed with "secrets referenced outside execute".

**Is it over-engineered?** It's strict on purpose, but it isn't arbitrary:
- It's deny-by-default. Each job's allowed write scopes are listed, and only `execute` may touch a secret.
- It exists so a powerful token can't leak into the job that runs on every push to main.
- A tiny edit does trip it, because any new secret or write scope has to be approved by editing the policy file. That is the intent, though it is annoying.

**My mistakes**
- My local verify ran only one of the workflow scripts, not the full `just workflow-contracts`. It passed locally and failed in CI. I've changed my verify to run `just workflow-contracts`. #483 passes it, exit 0.
- I proposed a fix that conflicts with a policy I hadn't read first.

**CI on the release PR, options now**
1. **Dispatch CI from the release job with `GITHUB_TOKEN`** (no secret). That needs `actions: write` on `version-pr`, which means loosening the policy, a security decision for you.
2. **Skip it.** Don't require CI on main. The merge queue and your bypass rights still apply, and the release PR is bot-built from changesets that already passed CI.

I recommend option 2. Option 1 adds permissions and complexity to guard against a rare failure.

**Other status:** #483's only red check is Entire Gates, which fails on missing reviewer approvals, not on code.

content.text:
Honestly: the secrets and permissions part is worth it, and it did its job here. The rest I'd call fair value at its current cost, but the cost isn't zero.

**What it guards against.** Callisto publishes to crates.io when the release PR merges, and a published crate can't be unpublished, only yanked. The policy script's rules cover:
- **Registry token:** `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` is only visible to the one job that publishes, and no other job can reference a secret.
- **Write scopes:** each job's write permissions are listed explicitly, so a new write scope can't slip in unnoticed.
- **Release source:** the publish job releases the verified merge commit of the release PR, not whatever is on main.
- **Target tables:** the hand-copied artifact tables (config, CI, build script, installer) must agree, so a new target can't ship half-configured.

**Did it earn its keep here?** Yes, on the secrets rule. I was about to put a repo-wide PAT into the job that runs on every push to main. That is the exact leak the rule exists to stop, and it's what the check caught.

**Is the cost worth it?** The check itself is cheap: one script, deny-by-default, with each failure line saying what to fix. Most of the work in this episode was mine. I didn't read the policy first, and my local verify skipped the script. The real cost to you is that legitimate changes, like a new secret or write scope, need a deliberate edit to the policy file, which is the point.

**What I'd trim.** The table-agreement checks are the likeliest to be noise in a repo with one product and five targets. Even they catch real drift, so I'd leave them unless they start firing without reason, which they haven't.

I wouldn't spend more effort on this. The CI-on-release-PR question is separate and still waiting on your option 1 or 2.

content.text:
Yes, CI on main is valuable, and I muddled two different things. CI already runs on main: `callisto-ci.yml` triggers on push to main and on `merge_group`. What I was chasing is narrower.

**The goal of B:** make CI a required check before merging, so a stale-green PR can't break main again, as happened once. That protects every human PR.

**Why #484 came up:** to require CI, every PR has to report those checks, and the bot-opened release PR #468 reports none. I assumed that would make it unmergeable and tried to make CI run on it.

**Where I overreached:**
- **Assumption:** I didn't test whether requiring checks actually blocks the release PR. Your repo has a merge queue, which runs CI on the merge-group commit, so it may be fine.
- **Workaround:** I built a fix for a problem I hadn't confirmed. The cheaper path was to require the checks and watch what happens to #468.

# Agent guide

Rules for AI agents working in this repo.

## Crates

| Crate | License | Depends on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| callisto-model | MIT | none (external: `michi-graph`, MIT) |
| callisto-manifests | FSL-1.1-MIT | model |
| callisto-graph | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests |
| callisto-cli | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests, graph |
| callisto-fixtures | FSL-1.1-MIT | model (dev-only) |

- `callisto-model` (MIT) must never depend on an FSL crate. It depends on `michi-graph` (MIT, no dependencies of its own) for dependency-graph validation and ordering. `just license-boundary` fails if anything it builds with is FSL.
- Check with `grep -H "^license" crates/*/Cargo.toml` after adding or moving a crate.

## Commands

- Full pipeline: `just ci` (includes the 90% coverage gate). `just test`, `just lint`, `just fmt`.
- Before every push or PR: `just pre-push && just lint && just doc-check && just test`, and `just ci` before marking a PR ready. Judge each by its exit code. Never tail or grep the output for success (a compile error prints no "failed" line), and never report a check as passed that was not run.
- Commits must be signed: the ruleset requires it. Never pass `-c commit.gpgsign=false`. After pushing, `gh api repos/orin-dx/callisto/commits/<sha> --jq .commit.verification.reason` must say `valid`.
- Performance: `just bench` times `status`, `version --dry-run` and `release --dry-run` over generated workspaces and counts the git processes each starts (`CALLISTO_BENCH_SHAPES=1` lists which). A change that adds a git process per package fails review.
- Scoped iteration: one `cargo test -p <crate>` or `cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets -- -D warnings` at a time.
  - Not `moon run <project>:test`: its per-project fan-out serializes on `target/`'s build lock.
  - Never run cargo builds in parallel.
- Changesets: `callisto add --package cargo/callisto-cli:<bump> --summary "..."` (non-interactive). Target `callisto-cli`: its changelog is the one users read. One changeset per user-visible topic. Lead with what the user sees now; add an action or limit when it matters. Use a short sentence for a simple change, or a short lead and bullets for related details. No internal names, mechanism or filler.
- Never `git checkout -- Cargo.lock` as cleanup. A lockfile diff means investigate, not discard.

## Invariants

1. Safe Rust only: `unsafe_code = "forbid"`.
2. Manifest edits preserve format: `toml_edit` for TOML; JSON changes that only replace string values are written into the original text by span (`json_text`), anything else keeps key order and fingerprinted indentation. No regex or line edits.
3. File writes go through `callisto_model::atomic::atomic_write`.
4. User-facing errors derive `miette::Diagnostic` with a code and a fix.
5. No emojis in docs or code.
6. No cargo features in shipped crates; behaviour is chosen at runtime (#143). The dev-only `callisto-model/test-util` feature is the exception.
7. No `unwrap()` outside tests (`just lint` denies it). An `expect` names the invariant that makes it unreachable.

## Fixing bugs

- Grep for structurally identical code (same algorithm, other file, ecosystem or mode). A sibling with the same defect is in scope now.
- N copies of one logic: unify to one implementation rather than patching each.
- A deliberately deferred sibling gets an explicit record: changeset note, tracked follow-up or code comment.
- A new shared helper migrates every call site in the same change, or the rest are tracked.

## Specs and plans

- Specs (`spec@1`) live in `docs/specs/`, one per area, current behavior only. Change the spec in the same PR as the behavior. No history, rationale or revision notes.
- This repo's release workflow has no GitHub Environment or reviewer gate and only `execute` gets registry secrets (owner policy, enforced by `.github/tests/verify-release-workflow-policy.sh`). Never add one.
- Read `ARCHITECTURE.md` and the matching `docs/architecture/` topic before changing behavior in an area.
- Read `docs/adr/README.md` before changing release flow, Git access, publishing, distribution, platform packages or manifest writes. Reversing an ADR needs a new ADR the owner accepts.
- Plans (`plan@1`) live in `docs/projects/`. Delete a plan once its work ships.
- Code never cites specs: no spec IDs, criterion IDs, section numbers or track names in comments, test names or messages. Describe the behavior instead.
- A requirement the owner didn't state is a judgment call. Get owner confirmation before it gates anything.

## Writing

- Succinct: short sentences, bullets, tables. No backstory, hedging or filler.
- Never hard-wrap Markdown or PR bodies: one line per paragraph.
- Code comments: one short line, only for a non-obvious why. Wrap at 120 columns (`rustfmt.toml`). No history ("used to", "previously"): git records it.
- No claude.ai session links in commits, PRs or files.

content.text:
Here is what I'd borrow from the well-known leaders. It's from memory of established practice, not fetched pages, so I can pull current sources to confirm any detail you want to rely on.

**What the best do**
- **Keep a Changelog:** write for humans, not machines, and never dump the git log. Group by what it means to the reader (Added, Changed, Deprecated, Removed, Fixed, Security), newest first, with the date.
- **Kubernetes:** the author writes the release note in the PR, in a required block, and reviewers review it with the code. A change that needs no note says so explicitly ("NONE"). Entries that need user action are called out as "action required" and surfaced at the top.
- **Stripe's API changelog:** each entry says what changed, who is affected and what to do. Breaking and non-breaking changes are marked, and migration guidance sits next to the change.
- **Rust and Go release notes:** the headline features get a few plain sentences, and often a short before and after example, grouped by area. Compatibility notes live in their own section.
- **Linear and Vercel:** lead with the benefit, keep it short, and show the thing.
- **Changesets-style tools:** the summary is addressed to consumers, and a major bump must carry migration guidance.
- **Cautionary tale:** changelogs generated from commit messages read like developer logs. That's what ours risked becoming.

**What that means for Callisto**
1. **Write the changeset in the PR and review it there.** Kubernetes treats the note as part of the change. We could add a "Changelog" line to the PR template, with "no changeset needed" as an explicit choice.
2. **Lead with the benefit, then the detail.** The first line is what a user would say to a colleague, and bullets hold the specifics.
3. **Mark who must act.** `Breaking:` and `Action:` already exist. The lesson is to make them the norm for anything that changes behavior, not an afterthought.
4. **Show, don't just tell, for headline features.** One before and after snippet beats a paragraph.
5. **Tier the release.** Highlights for the one or two things people should know, details below. 0.19.0 would have a single highlight: a much better release PR.
6. **Keep a single voice.** Pick one tense and mood, for example "Adds…", "Fixes…", "Now…", so the changelog reads as one document.
7. **Don't list fix-ups to unreleased work.** The cleanest changelogs only describe what a user can see.

I'd fold 2, 3, 6 and 7 into the changeset shape in AGENTS.md, with real before and after examples. I'd treat 1 and 5 as separate, bigger decisions for you.

Understood. We write principles and judgment, not length limits, and we fit the entry to what the reader needs.

**What I'd write down**
- **Audience first.** Each entry says what it means for someone upgrading, scripting or setting up, using sections when there is enough to say and one sentence when there isn't.
- **Scannable first, detail on demand.** A lead line gives the value, bullets give the specifics, and sub-bullets hold the depth for people who want it.
- **One entry per outcome, not per PR.** The last PR of a feature writes or updates the entry. A PR that isn't user-visible, or fixes something unreleased, gets no changeset.
- **Review means reading the rendered release PR as a user.** Don't just check that the files pass.

**Worked example (draft, nothing written to a file).** Here is what 0.19.0's release PR work could be as one entry, in place of five:

```
A release PR that tells you what to expect before you merge.

**What you see**
- Changes grouped under Major, Minor and Patch, each titled by its first line and linking its pull request (`#123`)
- A "Read before merging" block listing `Breaking:` and `Action:` notes, and packages that changed but aren't in this release
- Where merging will publish each package, with a warning if the release would be refused
- Labels such as `callisto: ready`, `blocked` and `bump: minor`, so you can triage without opening the PR

**Scripting**
- `callisto version --emit-preview <path>` writes the release as JSON
- `compose-pr-body --preview <path>` builds the PR body from that file
  - Relative paths resolve against `--cwd`

content.text:
Not terrible. It gets the audience right, but its shape conflicts with what you just described, so it needs changes. I read `courier:changeset-analyzer` 3.0.3 as installed. I haven't run it on our diffs yet, so this is a read of its instructions, not a test.

**What it gets right**
- It writes for a consumer deciding whether the change affects them, and bans engineering language ("refactored X") in summaries.
- It tells internal-only changes apart from user-visible ones.
- Breaking changes must say old behavior, new behavior and what the caller does.
- It warns against both bundling unrelated topics and fragmenting one effort.

**What conflicts with your direction**
- **Hard length caps.** The summary is capped at 200 characters, "one sentence for minor", "one clause for patch". That is the prescriptive target you don't want, and it would crush a feature like the release PR into one sentence.
- **Flat output.** The summary is a single string, so it can't produce a lead with sections, bullets and sub-bullets.
- **Per diff, not per outcome.** It splits a diff into topics, but one feature spans several PRs. It has no way to say "update the existing entry" or "this doesn't need a changeset".
- **No audience sections.** Nothing asks whether the entry matters to someone upgrading, scripting or setting up.
- **No required "why it matters".** The agent's own backstory complains about release notes that say what changed but not why, yet the output rules don't require the why.

**One thing to verify.** The agent says to load `shared/references/delivery/changesets.md` first, and I didn't find it in the 3.0.3 install. I saw a path that looks like it is under a codex copy of the plugin. If it's missing from the installed one, the agent runs without its decision table.

**What I'd change**
1. Replace the length caps with a principle: detail proportional to what a reader needs.
2. Let the summary carry a lead plus optional sections and bullets.
3. Add outcome-level granularity: update an existing entry, or recommend no changeset.
4. Add the "why it matters" and "who needs to act" requirements, and a few before and after examples.
5. Check that the shared reference ships with the plugin.

I'd run it once on #483's diff first, so we change it based on evidence. That plugin is outside this repo, so editing it is your call.

content.text:
The courier agent is better than I was on one point, and its own rules got in its way on the rest. Its output for #483:

> The release PR now shows `#N` beside each change, linking the pull request that added its changeset; the `--emit-preview` file gains an optional `pr` field.

**Where it did well**
- It named the link and where it appears, which my versions never did.
- It found a limit users will hit: changesets pushed directly with no pull request get no link.
- It classed the change as a minor new capability, which is right.

**Where its instructions hurt it**
- **Length cap:** "one sentence for minor" plus the 200-character limit forced it to squeeze a user-facing change and a scripting detail into one line. It then left the direct-push limitation in a scratchpad that is never forwarded.
- **Missing why:** it never says why the link helps.
- **Missing reference:** the shared reference it is told to load first didn't resolve, so it had to search for it.
- **Wrong semver table:** the table is built for agents and schemas, with no rows for a CLI's flags, output or serialized files, so it had to map by analogy.

That matches my read: the plugin needs changes. It was written for per-diff, one-line summaries, not the layered, audience-aware entries you described.

**A draft for #483's changeset, not written to a file:**

```
Links each change in the release PR to the pull request that added it.

- Shown as `#123` next to the change, so you can open the review and discussion behind it
- A changeset added without a pull request (a direct push) gets no link
- For scripts: the `--emit-preview` file has an optional `pr` for each change
```

**Next steps, if you agree**
1. Change the plugin: drop the caps, allow a lead plus bullets and sections, add "why it matters" and "who must act", add CLI rows to the semver table, and fix the reference path. This is outside this repo, so it's your call.
2. Write the changeset set (#483 and #486) using the agent with the new rules, so the text comes from the agent rather than me.

1	# Wisp Plugins AI Agent & Skill Specification (`AGENTS.md`)
2	
3	This guide defines the top-level repository guidelines for AI coding agents (Claude Code, AGY, Cursor, Copilot, Codex) working on or utilizing the Wisp Plugins repository (`orin-dx/wisp-plugins`).
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 1. Authoritative Sources
8	
9	All hard rules for plugin and agent authoring live in one place:
10	
11	- [**`shared/constitution.md`**](./shared/constitution.md): EARS-format authoritative constraints. The fence all plugin development must stay inside. Read this first and last.
12	- [**`shared/agent-best-practices.md`**](./shared/agent-best-practices.md): Principles behind the constitution, explained with examples. Authoring-time only — never loaded by agents at runtime.
13	- [**`shared/debugging-laws.md`**](./shared/debugging-laws.md): Core proof laws, read-only investigation rules, Red-to-Green verification standards.
14	- [**`shared/harness-authoring.md`**](./shared/harness-authoring.md): Cross-harness change classification, native workflow boundaries, and required counterpart review.
15	- [**`docs/adr/README.md`**](./docs/adr/README.md): Index of accepted architectural decisions, each with a guardrail. Read the record before changing what its guardrail names; [`shared/references/architecture/decision-records.md`](./shared/references/architecture/decision-records.md) says when and how to write one.
16	- [**`shared/references/tooling/cli.md`**](./shared/references/tooling/cli.md): Capability-aware preferences for modern CLI tools, with repository-native commands and safe fallbacks taking priority.
17	
18	---
19	
20	## 2. Directory Layout Standard
21	
22	```text
23	plugins/<plugin-id>/
24	├── plugin.json                   <-- Plugin Manifest (id, version, skills, agents)
25	├── README.md                     <-- Purpose, trigger phrases, agent table, install
26	├── CHANGELOG.md                  <-- Semver history
27	├── skills/
28	│   └── <plugin-id>/
29	│       └── SKILL.md              <-- Skill definition (dispatch matrix, pipeline)
30	└── agents/
31	    ├── recon.md                  <-- haiku/low  — deterministic enumeration
32	    ├── scanner.md                <-- sonnet/med — pattern matching
33	    ├── adversary.md              <-- sonnet/med — adversarial verification
34	    └── exit-gate.md              <-- opus/high  — binding judgment
35	```
36	
37	A plugin defaults to one skill directory named after the plugin id, as above. IF the plugin's scope covers several genuinely independent, heterogeneous intents on the same artifact — not a linear pipeline invoked as one flow — `skills/<plugin-id>/` may split into `skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md` per skill instead. `courier`, `scribe`, `weaver`, and `mason` are examples. The skill-routing key is the directory name, not the frontmatter `name:` field. A new skill name defaults to a single lifecycle-stage word; only go to a specific compound name (`audit-spec`, not `scribe-audit`) when the bare word is ambiguous or collides with another plugin's existing skill name. See `shared/constitution.md`'s Plugin Structure and Skill Names sections.
38	
39	Agents are organized by **cognitive mode** (enumeration, tracing, adversarial, systemic, behavioral, judgment, repair) — not by pipeline position. See `shared/constitution.md` for the model/effort tier rules.
40	
41	---
42	
43	## 3. Quick Checklist for Adding New Plugins
44	
45	1. **Use `mason`** — run `scaffolder` to generate the full directory structure and stubs.
46	2. **5-part agent structure** — every agent body: `<constitution>` (copied byte-for-byte from an existing agent), `<backstory>`, `<goal>`, `<judgment>`, `<output>`. No `<role>` body sections. No `success_criteria` checklists.
47	3. **EARS in output only** — WHEN/IF/WHILE/WHERE notation belongs only in `<output>` contracts and never-do rules.
48	4. **Progressive context loading** — one `<load_first>` block per agent, naming only the focused references needed for its cognitive phase.
49	5. **Schema-first handoffs** — define `shared/schemas/<name>@<version>.json` before writing the agent that produces it.
50	6. **Abstract tool language** — "use your file reading tool", never `view_file`, `read_file`, or `Bash tool`.
51	7. **Instruction economy** — keep one actionable rule per item, remove repeated rationale, and number only order-dependent work.
52	8. **Radical candor** — state material concerns, evidence, consequence, and confidence directly; do not soften blockers, manufacture praise, or overstate certainty.
53	9. **Reference routing and quality** — organize by cognitive concern, use language filenames only for language-specific evidence, and state outcome, applicability, evidence, refutation, and disposition.

# Wisp Plugins AI Agent & Skill Specification (`AGENTS.md`)

This guide defines the top-level repository guidelines for AI coding agents (Claude Code, AGY, Cursor, Copilot, Codex) working on or utilizing the Wisp Plugins repository (`orin-dx/wisp-plugins`).

---

## 1. Authoritative Sources

All hard rules for plugin and agent authoring live in one place:

- [**`shared/constitution.md`**](./shared/constitution.md): EARS-format authoritative constraints. The fence all plugin development must stay inside. Read this first and last.
- [**`shared/agent-best-practices.md`**](./shared/agent-best-practices.md): Principles behind the constitution, explained with examples. Authoring-time only — never loaded by agents at runtime.
- [**`shared/debugging-laws.md`**](./shared/debugging-laws.md): Core proof laws, read-only investigation rules, Red-to-Green verification standards.
- [**`shared/harness-authoring.md`**](./shared/harness-authoring.md): Cross-harness change classification, native workflow boundaries, and required counterpart review.
- [**`docs/adr/README.md`**](./docs/adr/README.md): Index of accepted architectural decisions, each with a guardrail. Read the record before changing what its guardrail names; [`shared/references/architecture/decision-records.md`](./shared/references/architecture/decision-records.md) says when and how to write one.
- [**`shared/references/tooling/cli.md`**](./shared/references/tooling/cli.md): Capability-aware preferences for modern CLI tools, with repository-native commands and safe fallbacks taking priority.

---

## 2. Directory Layout Standard

```text
plugins/<plugin-id>/
├── plugin.json                   <-- Plugin Manifest (id, version, skills, agents)
├── README.md                     <-- Purpose, trigger phrases, agent table, install
├── CHANGELOG.md                  <-- Semver history
├── skills/
│   └── <plugin-id>/
│       └── SKILL.md              <-- Skill definition (dispatch matrix, pipeline)
└── agents/
    ├── recon.md                  <-- haiku/low  — deterministic enumeration
    ├── scanner.md                <-- sonnet/med — pattern matching
    ├── adversary.md              <-- sonnet/med — adversarial verification
    └── exit-gate.md              <-- opus/high  — binding judgment
```

A plugin defaults to one skill directory named after the plugin id, as above. IF the plugin's scope covers several genuinely independent, heterogeneous intents on the same artifact — not a linear pipeline invoked as one flow — `skills/<plugin-id>/` may split into `skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md` per skill instead. `courier`, `scribe`, `weaver`, and `mason` are examples. The skill-routing key is the directory name, not the frontmatter `name:` field. A new skill name defaults to a single lifecycle-stage word; only go to a specific compound name (`audit-spec`, not `scribe-audit`) when the bare word is ambiguous or collides with another plugin's existing skill name. See `shared/constitution.md`'s Plugin Structure and Skill Names sections.

Agents are organized by **cognitive mode** (enumeration, tracing, adversarial, systemic, behavioral, judgment, repair) — not by pipeline position. See `shared/constitution.md` for the model/effort tier rules.

---

## 3. Quick Checklist for Adding New Plugins

1. **Use `mason`** — run `scaffolder` to generate the full directory structure and stubs.
2. **5-part agent structure** — every agent body: `<constitution>` (copied byte-for-byte from an existing agent), `<backstory>`, `<goal>`, `<judgment>`, `<output>`. No `<role>` body sections. No `success_criteria` checklists.
3. **EARS in output only** — WHEN/IF/WHILE/WHERE notation belongs only in `<output>` contracts and never-do rules.
4. **Progressive context loading** — one `<load_first>` block per agent, naming only the focused references needed for its cognitive phase.
5. **Schema-first handoffs** — define `shared/schemas/<name>@<version>.json` before writing the agent that produces it.
6. **Abstract tool language** — "use your file reading tool", never `view_file`, `read_file`, or `Bash tool`.
7. **Instruction economy** — keep one actionable rule per item, remove repeated rationale, and number only order-dependent work.
8. **Radical candor** — state material concerns, evidence, consequence, and confidence directly; do not soften blockers, manufacture praise, or overstate certainty.
9. **Reference routing and quality** — organize by cognitive concern, use language filenames only for language-specific evidence, and state outcome, applicability, evidence, refutation, and disposition.
10. **Verification evidence** — match checks to risk; require generators and oracles, independently derived semantic candidates, fresh state, terminal results, and explicit gaps when relevant.
11. **Cross-harness review** — preserve identity, skill routes, artifact contracts, evidence, and acceptance intent in Claude/AGY and Codex sources; native wording and delegation may differ.
12. **Manifest registration** — add an entry to root `marketplace.json` and validate: `jq . marketplace.json`.
13. **Legal attribution** — set `"author": "Gabriel Castro (Orin DX)"` in `plugin.json`.

---

## 4. Validation

```bash
just check
```

`just --list` shows each check as its own recipe (`just manifests`, `just test`, `just versions`, `just skills-doc`, `just reference-size`, `just marketplace-check`, `just mermaid`) for running a subset while editing; run the full set before release. `just fmt`/`just fmt-check` format with `oxfmt`; not yet part of `just check` until the repo has a baseline format pass. Generated Codex files in `.agents/plugins/` and `dist/codex/` must match their authored sources; never edit them directly — run `just marketplace-sync` after a Codex source change.

# Changesets

## Outcome

Record one coherent consumer-facing change in `changeset@2` so release tooling can preserve its meaning and calculate semver without reinterpreting prose. See `shared/schemas/changeset@2.json`.

## Consumer impact

| Value | Use when |
| :--- | :--- |
| `behavior-change` | Existing observable behavior changes for a consumer |
| `new-capability` | A consumer can do something new |
| `internal-only` | No behavior changes outside the repository |

`release-summarizer` omits `internal-only` entries from consumer release notes.

## Topic boundary

Use one changeset per independently releasable topic. Use these signals in priority order:

1. A shared linked requirement, spec, or plan defines one scope.
2. The author explicitly identifies a coordinated delivery scope.
3. The live diff shows one part exists because of another.

Do not split one outcome by package or file count. Do not bundle changes that could ship independently merely because they share a branch. When the boundary remains uncertain, state the ambiguity in `reasoning` and prefer the split that preserves accurate impact classification.

Verify `consumer_impact`, `semver_impact`, changed files, tests, and criteria evidence against that topic's own diff slice.

## Semver

| Change | Impact |
| :--- | :--- |
| Documentation or self-description only | `none` |
| Internal refactor or test-only change | `none` |
| Bug fix in runtime agent or skill behavior | `patch` |
| New optional schema field | `minor` |
| New schema or skill | `minor` |
| New plugin | `minor` |
| Removed or renamed schema field | `major`; create a new schema version |
| Renamed plugin ID or incompatible consumer behavior | `major` |

The release version is the highest `semver_impact` among included changesets. Classification comes from the structured field, not wording intensity.

## Breaking changes

Each breaking entry states:

- Old behavior.
- New behavior.
- Required consumer action.

Do not call an internal implementation change breaking unless it changes a supported consumer contract.

## Voice

Lead with observable consumer impact. Include a reason only when it changes understanding or action. Omit internal agent, file, and implementation detail unless the consumer must know it. State limitations and migration work directly. Full standard: `shared/references/authoring/voice.md`.

## Changeset, commit, and release note

| Artifact | Reader | Focus |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Commit | Maintainer reading history | Technical outcome and non-obvious reason |
| Changeset | Package consumer and release tooling | Observable impact and semver |
| Release note | Consumer deciding whether or how to upgrade | Grouped impact and required action |

Write a changeset when a PR changes runtime behavior, adds a consumer capability, changes a model or effort tier, changes a shared schema, adds a skill or plugin, or changes a verification protocol. Skip documentation, reference-only, internal refactor, and test-only changes unless they alter runtime instructions consumed by an agent.

## Release shape

```markdown
## v2.0.0 (2026-08-04)

### Breaking Changes
- Old behavior → new behavior. Required action.

### New Features
- Consumer-visible capability.

### Bug Fixes
- Corrected consumer-visible behavior.
```

# Courier — Changeset

<overview>
A changeset is the changelog entry, written once at authoring time and later aggregated — not rewritten — into a release. `changeset-analyzer` first checks how many independent topics the diff actually contains, then classifies consumer_impact and semver_impact per topic before writing anything, and scales each summary's detail to match: terse for a patch, one sentence for a minor, full old-behavior-to-new-behavior-to-required-action detail for a major. Delegates entirely to `changeset-analyzer`.
</overview>

<dispatch>
| Agent | Model / Effort | Delegate When |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **changeset-analyzer** | sonnet / medium | A git diff needs one or more structured `changeset@2` entries with consumer/semver classification and acceptance criteria mapping. |
</dispatch>

<references>
`shared/references/delivery/changesets.md` — changeset format, the Consumer Impact Classification table, the Semver Decision Guide, and the voice standard for this artifact.
</references>

<io>
**Consumes**: git diff (a single PR's, or a larger backlog/catch-up diff since the last release), optionally a linked `spec@1`, optionally smith's aggregated `criteria_evidence`
**Produces**: one or more `changeset@2` entries conforming to `shared/schemas/changeset@2.json` — one per independent topic found in the diff, never one entry bundling unrelated topics together. Route to `courier/pr` or `courier/release` depending on the next stage.
</io>
# Documentation Voice

Write for the person who must use, review, or maintain the artifact. Be succinct, friendly, direct, and technically honest.

## Choose the reader

| Artifact | Lead with | Include when relevant |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| User guide or README | What the user can do and when to use it | Prerequisites, examples, limits, recovery |
| Contributor or architecture doc | System responsibility and decision | Boundaries, invariants, tradeoffs, evidence |
| PR or review | Outcome and approval-relevant risk | Verification, gaps, migration, follow-up |
| Changeset or release note | Observable consumer impact | Old behavior, new behavior, required action |
| Decision record | The decision and the alternative rejected | Context, the causal because, consequences, enforcement, supersession |
| Reference | Decision the guidance supports | Applicability, evidence, refutation, disposition |

Use the reader's language. User-facing docs describe tasks and outcomes before internal agents, schemas, or implementation details. Contributor docs may use precise engineering terms when those terms help the reader act.

## Voice

- Lead with the outcome. Add context only when it changes understanding or action.
- Use active voice, present tense, and second person for instructions.
- Prefer familiar, concrete words. Define unavoidable domain terms once.
- Keep one main idea per sentence and one actionable rule per list item.
- Be friendly without ceremony: respectful, calm, and helpful; no praise, apology, or enthusiasm added as padding.
- Practice radical candor: state the concern, evidence, consequence, and confidence. Label blockers plainly. Do not manufacture praise, hide impact behind soft language, or imply certainty the evidence does not support.
- State mechanisms, behavior, and observed results instead of promotional adjectives.
- Let length follow the reader's need. Preserve non-obvious rationale, constraints, migration steps, and risks.

## Structure

- Use the smallest form that makes the relationship clear: prose for one connected idea, bullets for short parallel items, tables for repeated fields, and diagrams for structure or flow.
- Split a bullet when it contains independently actionable rules. Convert it to prose when its explanation is more important than enumeration.
- Use numbered steps only when order affects correctness.
- State a rationale once, next to the decision it changes.
- Link to authoritative detail instead of copying it.

## Cut

- Conversational preambles, scene-setting, and process narration.
- Restatements of a title, signature, diff, table, or preceding sentence.

# Task: make courier's changeset guidance produce layered, user-valuable entries

Repo: `~/projects/wisp-plugins` (orin-dx/wisp-plugins). Work in a git worktree off `origin/main`, not in the main checkout, which has the owner's uncommitted changes. Commits must be signed (never override signing). Read `AGENTS.md`, `shared/constitution.md` and `docs/adr/README.md` first. Edit authored sources only (generated Codex output is built with `just marketplace-sync`). Finish with `just check` passing and judge it by exit code.

## Why this exists

A Callisto maintainer (Callisto is a release tool) kept writing poor changesets. We tried `courier:changeset-analyzer` on a real diff (a feature that links each change in a release PR to the pull request that added it) and the agent's own rules got in its way:

- **Hard length caps.** The `changeset@2` schema has `summary.maxLength: 200` with "one clause for patch, one sentence for minor". The agent and `courier/changeset` skill repeat it. The agent had to choose between the visible change and a scripting detail, and left a real user-facing limitation (changesets pushed directly get no link) in `reasoning`, which is never forwarded.
- **Flat output.** `summary` is one string, so it cannot carry a lead line plus sections, bullets and sub-bullets.
- **Per-diff granularity.** The agent splits a diff into topics. Real features span several PRs, and some PRs need no changeset at all. Nothing lets it say "update the existing entry" or "no changeset needed".
- **No "why it matters".** The agent's own backstory complains about notes that say what changed but not why, but the output contract doesn't require it.
- **Semver table gaps.** `shared/references/delivery/changesets.md` has rows for agents, skills and schemas only. It has none for a CLI's flags, output formats or serialized files, so the agent mapped by analogy.
- **Reference not loading.** `load_first` names `shared/references/delivery/changesets.md`. In source this resolves through a `plugins/courier/shared -> ../../shared` symlink. The installed Claude copy (`~/.claude/plugins/cache/orin-dx-agent-plugins/courier/3.0.3/`) has no `shared/` at all, so the reference may never load.

## What the maintainer wants (use these as the design goals)

Changelog entries communicate value clearly to users who are upgrading, scripting or setting up. They are easy to scan and still give depth for readers who want it.

- **No hard length targets.** Prescriptive limits don't produce value with LLMs. Replace them with judgment: detail proportional to what the reader needs.
- **Layered structure when there is enough to say:** a lead line stating the value, then bullets, with sub-bullets for depth, grouped under audience sections where useful (for example what you see, scripting, upgrading). A one-line entry is fine when that is all there is.
- **Say what it is, why it helps, and what to do.** Name the visible thing (a "link", a "label", a "flag"), where it appears, and the action if any. Vague verbs like "identifies" or "says" fail this test.
- **State limits that users will hit.** They belong in the entry, not in a scratchpad.
- **One entry per user-visible outcome, not per PR.** A feature across several PRs updates one entry. A change that is not user-visible, or fixes something not yet released, gets no changeset. The agent should be able to recommend this.
- **Consistent voice** across entries, following `shared/references/authoring/voice.md`.

## Outcomes (definition of done)

1. `changeset@2` (or a new `changeset@3` if the change is breaking for consumers; follow the repo's schema-versioning rules) allows a layered summary without a length cap, and its description matches the new behavior. Decide with the ADR/constitution rules whether this is a new schema version, and justify it.
2. `agents/changeset-analyzer.md` and `skills/changeset/SKILL.md`: remove the "one clause / one sentence / 200 chars" rules. Add the audience, why-it-matters and action requirements, the outcome-level granularity (update an entry, or recommend none), and "limits belong in the entry". Keep the 5-part agent structure and byte-identical constitution block. Follow instruction economy: one actionable rule per item, no repeated rationale.
3. `shared/references/delivery/changesets.md`: add semver rows for CLI surface (new flag or command, changed output or exit code, new or changed serialized file) and a short worked example of a layered entry plus a bad-versus-good pair. Keep it under the reference size cap (`just reference-size`).
4. Downstream consumers (`release-summarizer`, `pr-narrator`, sentinel, anything that reads `changeset@2`) still work with the new summary shape; update them and their tests.
5. Add or update tests in `tests/` so the new schema and contract are covered.
6. Bump versions and CHANGELOG for the affected plugins per repo rules (`just versions`).

## Separate investigation, report only, do not fix in this change

Confirm whether Claude installs lose the `shared/` symlink: compare the source plugin dir with `~/.claude/plugins/cache/orin-dx-agent-plugins/courier/3.0.3/`. If `shared/` is missing there, every agent's `load_first` references and schemas fail to load in installed plugins, which affects all plugins. Describe the evidence, the likely cause (ARCHITECTURE.md says Codex bundles dereference symlinks but nothing is said for Claude), and options. Return it as a finding.

In practice, Claude sessions wrote changesets, commit messages and PR text freehand instead of calling the courier agents. Propose and implement, within this repo, the lightest way to make the right agent the default: sharper trigger wording in the `changeset`, `commit` and `pr` skill descriptions, and a short note in the courier README on when to use each. Do not add Claude hooks (the owner finds them too heavy). Anything that needs changes in the Callisto repo, such as its AGENTS.md or PR template, goes in your report as a recommendation, not a change.

## How to work

- Use mason's agents (`mason:scaffolder` and `mason:auditor`) or the repo's own checks to validate structure; do not invent your own format.
- Test the result: run `courier:changeset-analyzer` on this diff, a real Callisto PR diff (`gh pr diff 483 --repo orin-dx/callisto`) and confirm the entry names the link, where it appears, why it helps, and the direct-push limit.

---
callisto-cli: minor
---

The release PR tells you what to expect before you merge.

**What you see**
- Changes grouped under Major, Minor and Patch, each titled by its first line instead of its file name, with long notes folded away
- A "Read before merging" block listing `Breaking:` and `Action:` notes, a `Breaking:` note whose bump is too low, and packages that changed but are not in this release
- Where merging will publish each package, with a warning if the release would be refused
- Labels such as `callisto: ready`, `blocked` and `bump: minor`, so you can triage without opening the PR
  - Missing labels are created, and labels that stop applying are removed

**Scripting**
- `callisto version --emit-preview <path>` writes the release as JSON
- `compose-pr-body --preview <path>` builds the PR body from that file
  - Relative paths resolve against `--cwd`
- `compose-pr-body --publish-plan` adds the publish section; the release PR action already passes it

**Upgrading**
- Nothing to change. Start a changeset paragraph with `Breaking:` or `Action:` to have it listed.

content.text:
The error handling is strong, and I found one small gap worth a PR later. This was a read-only pass in a scratch repo, with no files changed.

**What I tried and how it went**
- **Unknown package** (`cargo/libb`): "E102 package not found in the workspace", with a hint to check the name and ecosystem.
- **Bad severity, missing ecosystem, empty summary:** each gives a coded error with a concrete next step. For example, "write the ecosystem and name with a slash, such as `cargo/lib`".
- **`release --dry-run` on a crate with no license or description:** a clear E323 pre-flight that says "Nothing has been published". A new user would otherwise find this out at publish time, so that's real value.
- **Mistyped command** (`relase`): suggests `release` and `release-pr`.
- **Scripted `add` for an npm package, `status`, `version --dry-run`:** all clear.

**The gap.** For `cargo/libb`, E102 says the package wasn't found but doesn't say what you probably meant. In a monorepo with dozens of packages a typo is common, and the user has to run `status` to find the right name. A "did you mean `cargo/lib`?" line, or a short list of close matches, would turn a retry into a one-step fix. The change is small and self-contained.

I'm not opening it yet, because #485 and #486 are still awaiting review. I'll start it as soon as one merges, so we keep to one open PR at a time.

Description:
Every push to `main` since 2026-11-02 18:07Z fails the Release workflow at "Derive and hash intent" with `E165: no changeset was consumed by this commit`. Nothing was published: no `0.17.0` tag, GitHub release or crates.io version exists, and the latest is `0.16.0`.

What happened. Release PR #409 was built from eight generated-name changesets (`gentle-tigers-leap.md` and others). #420 (merged 16:49Z) deleted those eight and added topic-named ones. The release workflow should have refreshed #409 on that push, but its "Create or update the Callisto release PR" step failed at 16:57:39Z with `gh: Something went wrong while executing your query` (GitHub request ID 2445:25D0C1:8E695E:1D11C81:6AE8C100), right after printing the 0.17.0 version plan. #409 stayed stale and was merged at 18:07Z. Its eight deletions were already on `main`, so the merge deleted nothing, left every topic changeset pending, and still applied the `0.17.0` bumps, changelogs and `release-decision.json`. The release commit consumed no changesets, and every later push retries it and fails the same way.

Cause, in layers. The trigger was a transient GitHub GraphQL error. `create-or-update-release-pr.sh` has no retry on its forge calls (`gh pr list`, the `createCommitOnBranch` mutation, the ref moves, `gh pr edit`), only on the final verify loop, and the workflow runs only on pushes to `main`, so one failed refresh leaves the release PR stale until the next push. Nothing stops a stale release PR from merging: E165 is only raised after the merge, and recovery is a manual revert.

### Minor Changes

- The release PR now links each change to the pull request that introduced it. The link, such as `#123`, sits next to the change, so you can open the discussion and review behind a line without searching for it.

  - The release date, plus a link to compare with the previous version when the GitHub repository is known
  - A package with no changes of its own, released only because its fixed or linked group was, gets one line saying so

  - To keep the old single list, set `layout = "flat"` under `[changelog]` in `callisto.toml`.
- The release PR tells you what to expect before you merge.

  **What you see**
  - Changes grouped under Major, Minor and Patch, each titled by its first line instead of its file name, with long notes collapsed into an expandable block
  - A "Read before merging" block listing `Breaking:` and `Action:` notes, a `Breaking:` note whose bump is too low, and packages that changed but are not in this release
  - Where merging will publish each package, with a warning up front if the release would fail, so you find out before merging
  - Labels such as `callisto: ready`, `blocked` and `bump: minor`, so you can triage without opening the PR
    - Missing labels are created, and labels that stop applying are removed

  **Scripting**
  - `callisto version --emit-preview <path>` writes the release as JSON
  - `compose-pr-body --preview <path>` builds the PR body from that file
    - Relative paths resolve against `--cwd`
  - `compose-pr-body --publish-plan` adds the publish section; the release PR action already passes it

  **Upgrading**
  - Nothing to change. Start a changeset paragraph with `Breaking:` or `Action:` to have it listed.

### Patch Changes

- Relative file flags of `release` and `release-pr` now follow `--cwd`.

  - Before, they resolved against the directory you ran from.
  - If a script passes relative paths together with `--cwd`, make them relative to that directory or absolute.
